b: How a Gitoodo release is built, checked and published (#152, #153, #562, #564). Users download an installer; building from source stays the fallback for people who want it. Assets All files land in target/release/dist/ on the Mac (the Windows files are copied there). File For Signing Gitoodo-<version>-macos-arm64.dmg Download button, macOS 11+ on Apple silicon Developer ID, notarized, stapled (DMG and app) Gitoodo-macos-arm64.zip install.sh (one-line install and update) the same notarized, stapled app Gitoodo-<version>-windows-x64.msix Download button once signed, Windows 10 2004+/11 x64 (per-user MSIX) MSIX signature; publisher = certificate subject Gitoodo.appinstaller MSIX with automatic updates (always names the newest MSIX) – (Windows checks the MSIX's signature) Gitoodo-<version>-windows-x64-setup.exe Windows 10/11 x64 per-user NSIS setup, no admin; download button while the MSIX is unsigned Authenticode when a certificate is set up, else unsigned gitoodo-aarch64-apple-darwin Remote Macs (#441, crates/core/src/remote_version.rs ) Developer ID, notarized (no staple for bare binaries) gitoodo-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc Remote Windows machines (#958); the CLI .exe , saved there as ~\.local\bin\gitoodo.exe Authenticode when a certificate is set up, else unsigned install.sh , uninstall.sh One-line install and removal on macOS – install.ps1 , uninstall.ps1 One-line install and removal on Windows (MSIX or setup) – ( install.ps1 checks the publisher) *.sha256 shasum -a 256 format ( <hash> <file> ) – releases.json Landing page download switch (schema below) – The names of the installers match what the landing page accepts ( site/src/release.ts : a .dmg for macOS; a -setup.exe , .msi or .msix for Windows). The unversioned zip keeps releases/latest/download/... working for install.sh . Linux CLI assets for remote machines ( gitoodo-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu , gitoodo-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu ) need a Linux build host and are not produced yet. Apple silicon only (decision 2026-11-16) Gitoodo for macOS ships for Apple silicon ( aarch64-apple-darwin ) only; there are no Intel ( x86_64-apple-darwin ) or universal builds. Reasons: macOS 27 is the last macOS for Intel Macs and Rosetta 2 ends with macOS 28, so macOS 27 already warns ("App-Update erforderlich") when an app starts Intel code on Apple silicon; and there is no Intel Mac to test on. What this means: release-mac.sh builds and checks ( lipo -archs = arm64 for every binary in the bundle) the arm64 app and CLI only; deny.toml lists no Intel Mac target. install.sh refuses a Mac without Apple silicon; it asks sysctl hw.optional.arm64 , so a Terminal running under Rosetta still counts as Apple silicon. Remote machines ( remote_version.rs , satellite_host.rs ) detect the system the same way ( uname -sm , corrected by sysctl on macOS). An Intel Mac gets the source intel_mac : the settings explain it ( hosts.versionIntelMac ) and offer no install, and nothing is downloaded. To check a build, use lipo -archs ; never run an x86_64 binary on an Apple silicon test Mac (it triggers the Rosetta warning there). Windows stays x64. Windows: MSIX and setup (decision 2026-11-16) Windows gets both, packed by release-windows.ps1 from the same signed binaries: MSIX ( src-tauri/windows/AppxManifest.direct.template.xml ) is the main download once a signing certificate exists. Per user, no admin; Windows removes the package with all its files, links and the gitoodo alias cleanly; updates come from Gitoodo.appinstaller (checked on launch, every 24 h and in the background; install.ps1 registers it); the publisher is shown and checked by Windows itself. Setup (per-user NSIS) stays: an MSIX installs only when signed by a certificate the machine trusts, so until the Windows certificate exists the unsigned setup (SmartScreen warning) is the only installer for normal users; it also runs on Windows 10 before 2004 and where sideloading of packages is blocked by policy. releases.json offers the setup first as long as the MSIX is unsigned. What the direct MSIX needs, and how it is solved: Need Solution One set of settings, logs, tokens Write virtualization off ( desktop6:FileSystemWriteVirtualization / RegistryWriteVirtualization = disabled, capability unvirtualizedResources , Windows 10 2004+): the app, the CLI and the services use the same %APPDATA% / %LOCALAPPDATA% folders as the setup install. Credential Manager is never virtualized. Background services Unchanged: gitoodo service install copies the CLI to %LOCALAPPDATA%\de.gitoodo.app\bin (outside the package) and registers the scheduled task Gitoodo\Daemon that runs that copy. Updates of the package do not touch it; the app refreshes the copy on launch (#529). gitoodo on the PATH Second application Cli with the execution alias gitoodo.exe (console subsystem) in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps . Start at sign-in The manifest's GitoodoStartup startup task; the direct build uses it when it runs packaged ( src-tauri/src/packaged.rs , autostart.rs ). A Run entry would name a versioned folder in WindowsApps that the next update removes. Notifications Packaged, the direct build posts through the package identity ( notify_windows.rs ), like the store build. Updates Gitoodo.appinstaller names releases/download/v<version>/Gitoodo-<version>-windows-x64.msix and lives at releases/latest/download/Gitoodo.appinstaller ; a newer package must carry the same publisher. The in-app update check still links to the release page. Uninstall Settings → Apps removes the package but cannot run anything first (MSIX has no uninstall hooks): a registered background service, settings and tokens stay. uninstall.ps1 removes the package ( Remove-AppxPackage ) and all of that, and checks for leftovers. Identity: de.gitoodo.app (the store build has its own Partner Center identity; both can be installed side by side and share the data of the direct build only through the unvirtualized folders). Switching between MSIX and setup with install.ps1 -Package removes the other install first and keeps settings, tokens and services. Checked on a Windows 11 x64 PC (2026-11-16) with a self-signed test certificate, removed afterwards: release-windows.ps1 -SignCommand … builds a signed setup and a signed MSIX (both binaries inside signed; MakeAppx accepts the manifest); install.ps1 with the local MSIX checks checksum and publisher and installs it; gitoodo --version runs through the alias; gitoodo service install from the packaged command puts the stable copy into the real %LOCALAPPDATA%\de.gitoodo.app\bin and starts Gitoodo\Daemon ; Credential Manager is read from the package ( token-access → readable ); the app runs with its package identity and writes only to the real data folders (nothing in the package's LocalCache ); the App Installer file registers its update settings; switching MSIX → setup → MSIX keeps services, settings and tokens; uninstall.ps1 removes all of it and -Check finds nothing. Not checked: the startup task and notifications in the UI, an update from a newer .appinstaller over HTTPS. Add-AppxPackage needs an interactive sign-in session (over SSH it fails with 0x80070005 ). Homebrew (prepared, not published) packaging/homebrew/gitoodo.rb is a cask template in the usual style of a project's own tap: the versioned DMG URL, livecheck on the latest GitHub release, Apple silicon and macOS 11 as requirements, the gitoodo command as binary , uninstall launchctl: for the LaunchAgents and a zap list. Publishing it means a tap repository silvio-l/homebrew-gitoodo ( brew install --cask silvio-l/gitoodo/gitoodo ) and, per release, version and sha256 from releases.json ( downloads.mac ); brew style passes on the template. A winget manifest ( InstallerType: msix ) can follow once the MSIX is signed. App identifier (decision 2026-11-16, #595) Gitoodo is de.gitoodo.app on every system: bundle ID, keychain group Q7V3X27S2U.de.gitoodo.app , service helper de.gitoodo.app.service , launchd labels de.gitoodo.app.{daemon,dispatcher} , folders, MSIX identity and AUMID, test build de.gitoodo.app.testaccess . It is written once per language: app_identifier! in crates/core/src/paths.rs (Rust derives labels, groups and paths from it), identifier in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json (Tauri, package.ps1 , release-windows.ps1 , build-local-mac.sh ), and the identifier variables of the install and uninstall scripts. Files that cannot derive it (Info.plists, entitlements, LaunchAgents, cask) are held equal by scripts/check-identifier.py in the gates and src-tauri/src/identity_files.rs ; the gate also fails on any identifier built from a person's name. Gitoodo 0.1.x used online.lindstedt.gitoodo . The first start of a newer direct build moves everything once ( crates/core/src/identity_migration.rs ): it stops and removes the old login items/LaunchAgents (Windows: scheduled tasks, Linux: user units), moves settings, state, logs, web data and the stable CLI copy (a rename; when the new folder already exists, entry by entry, never overwriting), copies the keychain tokens from the old access group into the new one, reads them back and only then deletes the old items, and registers the services again under the new labels with their previous on/off state. It is idempotent and safe to interrupt; it logs what it moved, never a value. The CLI moves the folders on service , status , doctor and diagnose for headless installs. Not moved: preferences and caches (rebuilt), the store and test builds. uninstall.sh , uninstall.ps1 and the cask remove both identifiers' leftovers. The App Installer of a 0.1.x MSIX cannot update across identities: such installs update by running install.ps1 again, which installs the new package and removes the old one (write virtualization is off, so no data goes with it). Credentials (names only, never in files or logs) macOS signing: the "Developer ID Application" identity of team Q7V3X27S2U in the login keychain ( APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY picks one when there are several). macOS keychain profiles (#594, docs/permissions.md "Keychain"): src-tauri/profiles/direct.provisionprofile (App ID de.gitoodo.app ) and src-tauri/profiles/service.provisionprofile (App ID de.gitoodo.app.service ), both Developer ID. With both, the build adds the service helper so the background services read tokens without a prompt; without them the release script warns. macOS notarization: an App Store Connect API key, APPLE_API_KEY (key id), APPLE_API_ISSUER (issuer id) and the key file ~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys/AuthKey_<id>.p8 ( APPLE_API_KEY_PATH overrides the path). When neither variable is set, release-mac.sh and ship.sh read ASC_KEY_ID and ASC_ISSUER_ID from ~/.appstoreconnect/asc_config (plain NAME=value lines, the convention of fastlane-style setups; APPLE_ASC_CONFIG overrides the path). The file is read, never sourced, and its values are never printed; the environment always takes precedence. Windows signing (optional for the setup, required for a usable MSIX): whatever the -SignCommand of release-windows.ps1 needs, e.g. Azure Artifact Signing (formerly Trusted Signing) through trusted-signing-cli with AZURE_CLIENT_ID , AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET , AZURE_TENANT_ID , or a certificate in the Windows store for signtool . The MSIX publisher is read from the signed app (or -MsixPublisher ); it must equal the certificate subject. Publishing: a GitHub token with contents: write on silvio-l/gitoodo (only for the last step). Microsoft Store upload ( fastlane windows_store ): a Partner Center (Microsoft Entra) app with tenant id, seller id, client id and client secret, stored once with msstore reconfigure (in CI from secrets); never in fastlane/.env . Ship scripts/ship.sh runs the whole release on the Mac, phase by phase, and is the checklist below. It is internal tooling (it drives the internal forge and the public export) and not part of the public source; the public pieces it uses are the scripts named in this document and .github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml . bash scripts/ship.sh --che

h: A block the human can decide from alone
b: This document is the single source of truth for the format that agents use to ask a human a question in a forge issue or comment, and for the answer comment that Gitoodo posts back. The parsers ( src/question/ and crates/core/src/question.rs ), the agent skill ( skill/gitoodo-questions/SKILL.md ) and the tests follow it. The examples below are extracted and parsed by a test, so they cannot drift from the parsers. Both question parsers read the examples directly from this document and compare their complete results against tests/question-examples.expected.json . When changing the format, update the examples and their shared expected results together; do not copy example inputs into another fixture. Version 2 replaces version 1; v1 blocks and answers are no longer read. The machine-read parts are fixed and English (markers, kind , Deadline: , Recommendation: , (yes/no) , (multiple) , (text) , the answer tokens yes , no , explain ). The human-read parts (the header line, context, questions, option labels, consequences, reasons) are written in the language Gitoodo writes in on the forge (en, de, es, ar, hi, zh-Hans): the setting "Language on the forge" (the app language, English, the issue's language or a fixed language), which a repository can override. "The issue's language" is read from the issue's title and body without code, links and mentions; when the text is short, mixed or in another language, the app language is used. Readers never depend on that language: answers are understood in every supported language ( yes , ja , sí , نعم , हाँ , 是 , …; see "Answer comment"). The format is an open standard: any agent, tool or forge integration may write and read it without Gitoodo. Its public, versioned home is https://gitoodo.com/spec/questions/v2/ , generated from this document when the site is built. Section anchors are the GitHub-style slugs of the headings ( #answer-comment , #tolerant-reading , #plain-answers ), so links into this document work the same in the repository and on the site. Compatibility promise Version 2 is stable. Within version 2 these never break: A block or answer comment that follows the exact grammar of this document stays valid and keeps its meaning: the markers, v2 , the id and kind attributes, the header, context, Deadline: , question, option and Recommendation: lines, the kind suffixes and the answer tokens ( 1b , 2 yes , 3 "text" , explain ). The machine-read parts stay English and keep their spelling; the block kinds worker , approval and clarification keep their meaning. A reader never demands more than this document demands today, so a writer that follows it is understood by every version 2 reader. The rule for detecting an answered question stays the same, and the forge remains the only source of truth. The one clarification (#764): a comment carrying a Gitoodo machine marker is never the human's reply, even under the human's login (see "Gitoodo comments"). The URL above and its section anchors stay valid for as long as version 2 exists. What may change within version 2: Tolerant reading may accept more slips, words and languages. It never changes how an exact block is read. Explanations, examples and the wording of this document may be clarified without changing a rule. How an app presents a card (layout, hints, controls) is not part of the format. Anything that would break a valid version 2 block or answer gets a new version with its own marker ( v3 ) and its own URL ( /spec/questions/v3/ ). The version 2 page stays published with its rules unchanged. Design goals Works on Forgejo, Gitea, GitHub and GitLab without any server-side support. Reads well as plain Markdown when the app is not used (a human can answer with a normal comment). Machine-readable: the app renders an answer card, the agent parses the answer. Agents write the exact format below; the app reads leniently (see "Tolerant reading") so that slips, hand-written questions and plain human answers still work. Anything that is not clearly a question stays plain text. Nothing ever crashes or half-renders. Question block A block is delimited by two HTML comments. HTML comments are invisible in the rendered Markdown of all four forges, and the text between them renders as normal Markdown (a numbered list with the options as lines below each item). <!-- gitoodo:questions v2 id="<id>" kind="<kind>" --> @<login> **<Name>** (<hint how to answer, e.g. `1b` or `2 yes`>) <up to 3 context lines> Deadline: <YYYY-MM-DD> 1. <Question>? a) <Option> – <consequence> b) <Option> – <consequence> Recommendation: a 2. <Question>? (yes/no) Recommendation: yes <!-- /gitoodo:questions --> Delimiters Opening: <!-- gitoodo:questions v2 id="<id>" kind="<kind>" --> . v2 is the format version; <id> matches [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64} and identifies the block inside its issue. The answer repeats it. <kind> is worker , approval or clarification (see "Block kinds"); both attributes are required, in this order. Closing: <!-- /gitoodo:questions --> . A body may contain several blocks. Ids must be unique per issue; for a repeated id the first block wins. Blocks inside fenced code blocks (``` or ~~~) are ignored, so documentation can quote the format. Block kinds The kind tells the orchestrator (and the app) why the question is asked. It never changes how the block is parsed or answered; the parsed block carries it as kind next to id . Kind Asked by Meaning worker an agent working on the issue The worker is blocked on a human decision and continues after it. approval the classifier A yes/no gate, e.g. for an issue or PR of an untrusted author. clarification the classifier The issue is contradictory or unclear ( needs-clarification ). Unmarked questions (found in running text) have the kind worker . Content All lines are optional, except at least one question. Part Syntax Notes Header @<login> **<Name>** (…) First line. Addresses the human; text after the bold part is free. A login that is no trusted person of the repo (unknown on the forge, no write access) counts as addressed to the user who reads the questions. Context up to 3 plain lines between header and first question More than 3 makes the block invalid. Deadline Deadline: YYYY-MM-DD Among the context lines; does not count as one. At most once. Question <n>. <text> with n = 1, 2, 3, 4 in order 1 to 4 questions per block. Option a) <label> or a) <label> – <consequence> Keys a to d in order. The dash is an en dash or - . Recommendation Recommendation: <value> below the question At most once. Agents should always give one (see the skill). Question kinds The kind is given by an optional suffix at the end of the question line. Kind Suffix Options Recommendation: value Answer token single choice none 2 to 4 ( a to d ) one key, e.g. a 1b or 1bc multiple choice (multiple) 2 to 4 ( a to d ) keys separated by commas: a, c 1ac yes/no (yes/no) none yes or no 2 yes free text (text) none not allowed 3 "any text" A recommendation may be followed by – <reason> ; the reason is ignored. A single choice asks for one option, but the human may combine several: a click in the app picks one option, and an option can be added on purpose (the card's "choose several" control or a Cmd/Ctrl-click). The answer then carries every chosen key like a multiple choice ( 1bc ). Agents read such an answer as "all of these options" (see the skill). The question block itself is unchanged: a single choice still has at most one recommended key. Answer comment The app posts one comment per answered block: <!-- gitoodo:answer v2 id="<id>" --> <answer line> <optional free text, Markdown> Line 1 is the marker with the same id as the block. Line 2 is the answer line: space-separated tokens, one per answered question, in question order: single or multiple choice: number plus the chosen keys in alphabetical order, no separator: 1b , 3ac ; yes/no: number, a space, yes or no : 2 yes ; free text: number, a space, then the text as a double-quoted JSON string ( \" and \n escapes): 4 "Berlin" ; "please explain better", for every kind: number, a space, explain , optionally a space and a note what is unclear as a double-quoted JSON string: 2 explain or 2 explain "What does staging mean here?" (see "Explanation requests"). Questions can be left out (partial answers are valid). Each number occurs at most once. After one blank line follows optional free text, the person's note ("Anmerkung"). It is plain Markdown and not interpreted (see "Notes"). An answer line that does not match this grammar makes the whole comment "not an answer" (it stays an ordinary comment). The tokens are case-insensitive when parsed; the app always writes the lowercase English tokens. Every supported language is understood when reading, in the answer comment and in plain answers: Meaning Words yes yes , ja , sí , si , نعم , हाँ , हां , 是 , 好 no no , nein , لا , नहीं , नही , 否 , 不 explain explain , erklären , explicar , اشرح , समझाएं , 解释 A word ends at whitespace, , , ; , . or a quote; digits and keys ( 1ac ) stay as described above. Explanation requests Instead of choosing, the human can send a single question back with <n> explain when the question, the options or the decision criteria are not understood. It is allowed for every question kind and can be combined with answers to the other questions of the same block ( 1b 2 explain "What does b cost?" 3 yes ). The optional note is a JSON string like a free-text answer; an empty note is written as no note. The agent re-asks exactly the questions marked explain in a new block (new id ) with a fuller explanation of the question, the options and the decision criteria, and keeps the other questions as answered. For the app the block counts as answered like after any other partial answer, so the question is no longer open until the new block arrives, which then shows up as a new question. Notes Every answer a person gives through the app may carry a note: the free text of an answer comment (a question or an approval, also when a whole group of approvals is answered at once) and the note of a finished task (see "Instructions"). Before it is posted the app trims it and normalises line ends to \n ; writes every <!-- as <!-- , so a note can never open a Gitoodo marker (an answer, a question block, the automation marker) or hide text; it renders the same; closes a code fence the note leaves open, so the fence cannot swallow the rest of the comment; caps it at 4000 characters, marking a cut with … . An empty note is left out. Readers take the free text as written; they never interpret it as an answer line. Gitoodo comments The orchestrator may write with the user's own account (no separate worker account), so the login alone cannot tell a worker's question or a status note from the human's reply. Every comment that Gitoodo, its dispatcher, its classifier or a worker posts therefore carries a machine marker on a line of its own: a question block ( <!-- gitoodo:questions v2 … --> ), a lease ( <!-- gitoodo:lease v1 ) or an intake marker ( <!-- gitoodo:intake-rejected --> , <!-- gitoodo:intake-milestone-created --> ), or else the automation marker as the last line: <!-- gitoodo:auto --> . A comment with any of these markers is written by Gitoodo, whatever account posted it. The answer marker ( <!-- gitoodo:answer v2 … ), the forward marker ( <!-- gitoodo:forwarded v2 … ) and the instruction marker ( <!-- gitoodo:instruction v2 --> , see "Instructions") belong to a human acting through the app; a comment with any of them is the human's, even when it also carries a question block (a forward). A comment without any marker is written by a person. For comments written before the automation marker existed, readers also treat these unmarked status notes as Gitoodo's: a comment that starts with gitoodo: , one that starts with Gitoodo could not bring this branch up to date with , and Milestone <name> is closed; removed from it (backlog). Writers other than Gitoodo (an agent asking through gitoodo ask or the skill) post

Every subcommand of the gitoodo command line, generated from the text gitoodo --help prints (the USAGE constant in crates/cli/src/main.rs ). The app installs the command with its background services; the daemon reference covers configuration and tokens. Synopsis usage: gitoodo next --worker <id> --host <host> [--repo <owner/name>] [--account <id>] [--json] gitoodo done --worker <id> --lease <id> [--result <text>] [--json] the lease commands the dispatcher works the queue with; from the command line they are refused in an automation session and for repositories whose autopilot is on (it works that queue) gitoodo status [--changed] [--json] [--ack] queue picture of all configured accounts --changed exit 0 when the waking lines changed since the last --ack, 1 otherwise --json machine-readable output --ack remember the current waking lines as seen gitoodo doctor diagnostics: where the daemon takes tokens from (systemd credentials, service environment, system keyring or memory only) and, per account, whether this terminal reads the token; when the keychain wants approval it names the ways on: the app's System check, token-access --grant, or GITOODO_TOKEN_<ID> gitoodo trace <owner/repo#n | run-id> [--local] [--output] timeline of one issue or run from the logs: every step from the classifier's decision over host choice, worktree, worker, pull request and checks to merge and cleanup, with durations; also asks the satellites for their lines (--local: this machine only); read-only, redacted; names the worker transcripts kept on this machine (--output: prints them) gitoodo diagnose [--hours <n>] summary of the last 24 hours (or n): runs, count and p50/p95 per step, top wait reasons, errors by kind, the log folder against its budget and the cleanup state (leftover worktrees and branches, disk, errors); read-only, redacted gitoodo clean [--dry-run] remove what coding agents keep of Gitoodo's runs whose worktree is gone (session transcripts, project and state folders), as the dispatcher does every round; --dry-run only lists it. The user's own sessions and the data of runs that may resume stay gitoodo token-access --account <id> [--grant] whether the background services read the account's token without a keychain prompt; prints readable, needsPrompt, missing or failed; --grant asks once so "Always Allow" can be chosen gitoodo token-purge remove every Gitoodo token from the data protection keychain (the uninstaller runs it through the service helper, which shares the app's keychain group); prints removed or unavailable gitoodo stop-all emergency stop: no new work, running workers are stopped and released (worktrees kept), no merges and no classifier writes until `gitoodo resume`; survives restarts gitoodo resume lift the emergency stop; every repo continues in the state it had before gitoodo usage [--refresh] [--json] usage limits of the coding agents as the dispatcher holds them (5-hour and weekly window, paused until); --refresh checks every agent now, on this machine and every worker machine (at most every 30 seconds), and a limit that is gone lets the workers start at once gitoodo release [--repo <owner/name>] [--json] release planning: open, in-progress and merged items of the next release (docs/orchestrator/release.md) gitoodo release-version --repo <owner/name> [--account <id>] [--json] [--check] suggested next version from the next release's issues and the last released version, with its reason; a script scheme runs the repo's script in the local checkout without a token; --check only checks the stored version config (docs/orchestrator/release.md) gitoodo release-rules --repo <owner/name> [--account <id>] [--json] release assignment rules in effect, their problems and the suggestions waiting for approval; h: Quitting the app and the services (#737)
b: gitoodo is the headless side of Gitoodo: the classifier daemon that polls the forges of the configured accounts and a command line that asks it for the queue picture. The app does not need it and works unchanged without it. Commands gitoodo status [--changed] [--json] [--ack] gitoodo service install|uninstall gitoodo classifier gitoodo next --worker session-1 --host win [--repo owner/repo] [--account id] [--json] gitoodo done --worker session-1 --lease <id> [--result "PR ready"] [--json] gitoodo usage [--refresh] [--json] status prints one line per open issue and pull request of the covered repos, grouped like the lage picture: repo, issue#N / pr#N , status labels, age bucket, warnings, title, and a summary line at the end. Issues without status labels show [ohne Einordnung] . --json prints the whole reply ( picture , changed , digest , polled_at , errors ). --changed prints nothing (unless --json ) and exits 0 when the waking lines changed since the last --ack or an issue lacks status labels, 1 otherwise. --ack stores the current state as seen. Typical wake check: gitoodo status --changed && gitoodo status --ack . usage prints the usage of each agent of the dispatcher (5-hour and weekly window, "paused until" at the limit); --refresh first has the dispatcher and every worker machine ask each agent again, as "Check limits now" in the app (at most once per 30 seconds, see docs/orchestrator/dispatcher.md , "Usage limits"). --json prints the providers. Exit code 2: the daemon is not reachable. 64: wrong usage. classifier runs the classifier daemon in the foreground; the service runs exactly this. daemon is a deprecated alias that runs the same thing and prints a note. Classifier role and read model The classifier (spec section 6) polls every repository in state observed (read only), paused and active ; repositories in state off are listed but never read. After each poll it builds a read model in memory and serves it to the app and the CLI over the local socket: request {"cmd":"read_model"} , reply {"reply":"read_model", ...} with polled_at and per repository account_id , full_name , state and the open issues, highest score first. After a start the request waits up to two minutes for the first poll; {"cmd":"read_model", "immediate":true} answers at once instead ( polled_at then is null and repos empty). The app always asks immediate and gives up after 15 s as busy , so a long first poll never keeps its views loading ( read_model_now ); per issue: number , title , html_url , labels , computed readiness ( ready , blocked , needs-clarification , needs-approval , needs-human , in-progress , in-review , stalled , held ), dependencies ( owner/repo#n ), cycle , score and the lease holder if any; readiness uses the dependency graph (open dependencies block, cycles and self-dependencies need clarification, unknown dependencies fail closed), the trust decision of section 5.3 and the label catalog; the score is the dispatcher order of section 7.1 with the weights of the score section of the orchestration config. Request {"cmd":"poll"} (reply {"reply":"poll_scheduled"} ) ends the wait between two polls; the app sends it after the user unlocked or granted a keychain token, so an account that waited for approval is read again at once. Each poll writes its errors to the activity file right before its poll record; rule notes such as "… more questions pending" go to the record's notes , never to labels_set . The types and the client ( ping , read_model , poll_now , request_at ) live in gitoodo_core::service_rpc . The classifier idles at a few MB; an integration test keeps it under 30 MB RSS without accounts. Queue writer and leases The daemon is the only Gitoodo process that writes status labels. next , done and label maintenance share one asynchronous lock, including their fresh forge reads. Run **one writer daemon per repository**; a second host must use that daemon, not start another writer for the same repository. An OS-held daemon.lock in the configuration folder prevents simultaneous writers for the same configuration, even during startup; the OS releases it after a crash. Exactly one classifier runs per configuration (#593, #600): While no service is registered, the app starts gitoodo classifier itself with its process id in GITOODO_PARENT_PID . That classifier (and a dispatcher the app starts) stops within two seconds once the app is gone (quit, crash, update), so the app leaves no orphan. Once the classifier service is registered, the app starts only the service, and a classifier the app started stops by itself and hands over. The service definitions set GITOODO_SERVICE=1 . A classifier service whose lock is still held waits for it instead of exiting, so launchd or systemd do not restart it in a loop; it logs took over the classifier lock when it does. Windows: the parent watch is Unix-only for now; the app's exit stops its children there. Worker identities live inside the local OS-user trust boundary; the dispatcher ([ orchestrator/dispatcher.md ](orchestrator/dispatcher.md)) is the only component that starts workers. Enable repositories explicitly in <config>/orchestration.json (Gitoodo's own configuration): { "repos": [ { "account_id": "nas", "full_name": "owner/repo", "human": "maintainer-login", "releases": true } ], "lease_seconds": 14400, "profile": { "names": {}, "extra_labels": [] } } Missing configuration keeps the daemon read-only. Invalid configuration blocks mutations. Accounts must exist in settings.json ; disabled repositories cannot be assigned. Maintenance runs during polling for enabled repositories, including those outside the dashboard view. next --repo selects an enabled, non-disabled repository. The daemon never edits the config; the only service that does is the dispatcher, which at its start only tidies former start-mode fields and keeps halted as it was. While halted is set, next returns no assignment and the maintenance pass writes nothing ([ orchestrator/dispatcher.md ](orchestrator/dispatcher.md), "Emergency stop"). next and done are the lease commands the dispatcher works the queue with. From the command line ( gitoodo next , gitoodo done ) they never compete with it (#953): in an automation session ( GITOODO_ISSUE is automation:<id> ) both are refused with the code automation_session : an automation reports, it does not take or finish issues; for a repository whose autopilot is on (state active ), next is refused with the code autopilot_on and names the repositories: the autopilot works that queue. done from the command line does not finish a lease in such a repository either (same code). The dispatcher's own requests are not affected; the command line marks its requests with "cli": true . next returns JSON with an assignment (or null when no work is eligible). An assignment contains the full issue and its lease: id, worker, host, account, repository, issue number, expiry and completion flag. Candidates must be open, carry only ready (legacy status:bereit ), have no prd , needs-human (the legacy name an:mensch is not recognised), stalled or extern , and either have no host restriction or a matching host: label. For --host local a host: label matches this machine's name ( orchestration.json › local_host.name , default the sanitised short host name), any of its local_host.aliases and local , without case — the same matcher as the dispatcher ( docs/orchestrator/spec.md , 7.1 item 3). Satellites match only their own configured name. A host: value that names no configured machine but a platform ( mac , win , ubu , ...; see spec 7.1) matches any host running that system. Candidates are taken in the order the app's queue shows (spec 7.1 item 4): the next release and boosted issues first, then by score (priority weight, age per hour, manual boost, release bonus, with the repository's own weights when it has them), highest first; ties go to the earlier creation time, then the lower issue number, then the configured account/repository order. Priorities are priority:p0 .. p3 (legacy prio:1..3 ); an issue without one counts as priority:p2 . Dependencies are declared by a line of their own, in the body or in a comment a person wrote. The line starts (after an optional list bullet - , * , + or 1. and optional bold ** ) with one of Depends on , Blocked by , Waits for , Wartet auf , Abhängig von , Blockiert bis , Abhängigkeit(en) , Depende de or Bloqueado por (any case), an optional colon, and the references, separated by commas, spaces, and or und : Wartet auf: #12, owner/other#3 - **Depends on:** #7 and #8 #12 , repo#12 and owner/repo#12 are supported, including nested GitLab namespaces; the list ends at the first word that is no reference. Anything else is no dependency: a mention in the middle of a sentence, a closing reference, a status line such as Worker fertig: PR #1382, wartet auf gate/nas. and every comment Gitoodo wrote itself (its machine marker, see [ question-format.md ](question-format.md)). A referenced issue or pull request must be verifiably closed or merged; an open, missing or inaccessible one blocks assignment. The app's queue uses the same rule and the same lookup, so such an issue shows as blocked there, never as the queue head. When the dispatcher passes over a ready issue for open dependencies it logs dispatch.skip ( reason dependencies_open , refs the blocking references) once per issue and change, so gitoodo trace owner/repo#n explains the wait. Assignment adds in-progress before removing ready , adds the forge account's authenticated login to the assignees (people already assigned stay; GitHub adds atomically, Gitea/Forgejo and GitLab write the fresh list plus the login), then writes a gitoodo:lease v1 audit comment naming the worker and lease. Worker ids identify sessions, not forge logins. A partial or ambiguous failure leaves the reservation in place. Claims are compare-and-confirm across installs (release-gate review M10): after its lease comment the writer reads the comments again. Every active (not completed, not withdrawn, not expired) lease comment of Gitoodo's own logins posted since the issue was read as ready (plus 10 s for request latency) belongs to the race; the oldest comment wins. The loser posts the same lease again with "withdrawn": true , removes only its own login from the assignees (and only when it added it and the winner is another login), leaves labels alone and backs off for this round. A withdrawn lease never holds an issue. Two installs only see each other's leases when their logins are known writers of the forge host (the same account, or listed orchestrator accounts). done verifies the current audit from the authenticated account (the newest lease comment whose lease was not withdrawn), changes the status to in-review , removes the worker account's assignee and records the result. On an issue that is already closed (the dispatcher closes it with the merge before it reports the run done) it removes in-progress / in-review instead of setting in-review (#848). Repeating an already completed report has no further effects. Leases are reconstructed from forge comments after a restart; they do not depend on the volatile SQLite cache. Rejected reports return JSON reply: "rejected" with a stable code and a human-readable message , exit status 1: foreign_lease , expired_lease , stale_lease , status_changed , invalid_worker , configuration_error , forge_unavailable (server error, rate limit or unreachable forge: worth retrying) or forge_error (any other forge refusal). Expiry is inclusive and never releases the issue automatically. Recovery of expired or partially assigned work is done by the dispatcher's sweeper or by an explicit human decision. A timed-out next may have taken effect; inspect the issue/audit before requesting more work. Label template and hygiene The default profile embeds the English label catalog ( priority:p0 .. p3 , os:* , host:* , needs-clarification , blocked , ready , in-progress , in-review , stal

h: Per mode: orchestrator, working directly, answering
When a new version needs more
b: Gitoodo needs a personal access token per account. The token wizard (Settings > Accounts > add) and the Replace token … dialog of a stored account name the permissions in the words of the forge's own token page, with the reason for each. This page is the same list for later. The wizard texts live in src/views/settings/permissionGuide.ts ; tests/token-permissions.test.ts fails when this page, the wizard and the checks in crates/core/src/forge drift apart. GitHub Classic token (Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens (classic)); the wizard opens the page with both boxes ticked: Permission Why repo Read repositories and issues, send answers as comments, close issues read:user Recognise which account the token belongs to Fine-grained token: choose the repositories under "Repository access" and set under "Repository permissions": Permission Why Metadata: Read-only List repositories (GitHub grants this automatically) Issues: Read and write Read issues, send answers as comments, close issues GitLab Permission Why api Read issues, send answers as comments, close issues read_api is enough for reading only; without api Gitoodo cannot answer. Forgejo and Gitea Forgejo and Gitea cannot preselect permissions by link. Set them by hand on the opened page (User settings > Applications): pick this access level for each category and leave all others on "No access". Category Access level Why user Read Recognise which account the token belongs to repository Read List the repositories of the account issue Read and write Read issues, send answers as comments, close issues Per mode: orchestrator, working directly, answering The lists above are what answering questions needs. The wizard asks what Gitoodo should do with the repositories, preselects the operating mode chosen in onboarding (or set in the app) and shows one merged list for that mode: each category once, the highest access level wins, plus the role the account needs in the repository. It goes on only after I have set these permissions on the token is ticked; switching to a mode that needs more asks again. The rights per mode come from crates/core/src/forge/rights.rs , the merge from src/views/settings/tokenBlock.ts . Forge Working directly Orchestrator, in addition Forgejo / Gitea repository : Read and write organization : Read and write, only to create or delete repositories in organisations GitHub classic — delete_repo , only to create or delete repositories GitHub fine-grained Contents: Read and write Pull requests, Administration, Commit statuses: Read and write (Administration also creates and deletes) GitLab — — ( api covers creating and deleting) Role in the repository Write (GitLab: Developer) Admin (GitLab: Maintainer), for repository settings such as merge styles and branch protection The organisation scope is optional (#978): Forgejo and Gitea refuse creating and deleting a repository that belongs to an organisation without write:organization , even when the token has write:repository ; GitHub classic tokens delete only with delete_repo . A token without it is still stored and works on every repository; the account in the settings names the gap ("Only to create or delete repos") with Replace token … , and the removal dialog names the scope before the delete is confirmed. A separate orchestrator (worker) account per forge host (#764, docs/orchestrator/spec.md 5.3.1) needs the orchestrator's rights without repository settings ( forge::rights::worker_rights ): no Administration permission and no admin role; write access (GitLab: Developer, Maintainer to merge into protected branches) is enough. Repository settings stay with the user's own account. Creating the worker account automatically ( docs/orchestrator/setup.md , "Automatic worker account") needs more on the own account, only for that moment: Forgejo/Gitea a site administrator whose token has write:admin ; GitLab self-managed an administrator token with api (and Admin Mode where the instance enforces it). Without them the step falls back to the guide; the own token is never asked to gain these scopes for anything else. The worker token it creates has exactly read:user , write:repository , write:issue (Forgejo/Gitea) or api with a 364-day expiry (GitLab). How the check finds out GitHub classic tokens list their scopes in a header and GitLab tokens on /personal_access_tokens/self . Forgejo and Gitea reveal nothing: reading scopes are probed with cheap reads, and the write scopes beyond answering ( write:repository , write:organization ) with a write the forge refuses: an empty body to POST /api/v1/repos/migrate and POST /api/v1/orgs . The forge checks the token's scopes before it reads the body, so a missing scope answers 403 with its name and a present one a validation error; nothing is ever created. Only a named scope counts as missing, so an older forge without scoped tokens reports nothing. GitHub fine-grained tokens reveal no permissions; there the forge names a missing one at the action. The wizard stores a token only when it gives everything the chosen mode needs (writing for working directly and the orchestrator); a token without the optional organisation scope is stored and the gap stays visible on the account. When a new version needs more The check runs when an account is added, its token replaced and synced, and again whenever the accounts in the settings open. If the stored token lacks a permission, the account shows what is missing and offers Replace token … . Replacing a token Replace token … sits on every account in Settings > Accounts (the key icon while the token is fine, a button while it is rejected, missing or short of permissions), on the scope hint and the sync error bar, in the repository rights check, the removal dialog, the status page and the worker account section. It opens a small dialog, not the wizard: one masked paste field (with Show ), a Create token on <host> link (GitHub and GitLab preselect the scopes; Forgejo and Gitea cannot) and the folded permission list. Save sends the token to the core, which: trims it and checks it against the forge; a network or forge error stores nothing; refuses a token of another user (logins compared case-insensitively) and names both logins; reads the scopes: a token without a scope the sync needs is refused, because the account would stop working; a token that only lacks scopes for answering or working is stored after Save anyway (Forgejo tokens cannot be edited later, a partial token beats a revoked one, and the account keeps the gap marked); missing scopes for creating or deleting repositories never stop it; stores it under the same keychain entry. If the write fails halfway, the old token is written back. Nothing is stored before steps 1 to 3 have passed. Afterwards the account's token error and banners clear, its sync restarts, the scope marks and the open rights checks run again. The account keeps its id and every setting; all repositories of the account use the new token, since they share the one keychain entry. The background services (classifier, dispatcher) read the token from the keychain on every cycle, so they use the new token from their next cycle without a restart. On macOS the app then grants the service helper access to the rewritten item where needed (restarting the services only if a grant changed something) and asks the classifier to poll now; on Windows the scheduled task reads the Credential Manager on its next cycle. A token handed to a headless service as GITOODO_TOKEN_<ID> or a systemd credential ( docs/daemon.md ) overrides the keychain and is replaced where it was set. Release rule: a version that adds a required permission lists it in the changelog under "Added" or "Changed" as "New permission required: ...", and the permission appears in the lists above. Closing can also be refused even with write permission: HTTP 412 means forge prerequisites are unmet, for example open issue dependencies. Gitoodo explains this and points to the issue in the browser; it does not remove dependencies or report the issue as closed.

t: States: what Gitoodo shows and what you do about it
h: 2. Issue: where a piece of work stands
3. Worker: one agent on one issue
4. Things Gitoodo repairs on its own
b: Gitoodo is an orchestrator: it takes issues from your forges, hands them to AI coding workers and brings their results back as pull requests. This page is the one map of that flow. Every mark in the sidebar, every session tile, every column in "All repos" and every line on the status page belongs to one of the states below, and each state says whether anything is asked of you (#870). The short version: you act only on "needs you" and "stuck" , and on "in review" when your merge setting leaves the merge to you. Everything else moves by itself: failing checks go back to the worker, and anything left behind is cleaned up by Gitoodo, not by you. 1. Repository: autopilot on or paused Every repository has one switch (#877), in the sidebar and in the settings. State Gitoodo reads Sets labels Starts workers What it means Autopilot on yes yes yes Gitoodo works the repository's issues Paused yes yes¹ no no worker starts; questions still show up ¹ Only in a repository the autopilot worked before; one it never worked stays untouched. "Asked of me" and every counter (header, sidebar, tray, notifications) list what waits for you in repositories with the autopilot on (#897). What waits in paused repositories or in repositories without the autopilot stays behind "N more from repos without autopilot – show" at the end of the list; Settings → Notifications → "Questions from repos without autopilot too" shows it for good. Direct mode always lists every repository. A repository you never want to see is removed from the sidebar ("Remove"); "Show again" in the settings brings it back. Pausing a repository stops its running workers. Their issues go back to ready (the in-progress label is removed), so pausing never leaves work behind. 2. Issue: where a piece of work stands The labels on the forge are the source of truth; the classifier sets them, the dispatcher reads them. A repository row in the sidebar shows at most two marks (#740): the rotating circle in front of its name while a worker runs there, and after its name the "needs you" mark, only while something needs you there (a question or approval, or a stuck issue), with the count when there are several. Everything the autopilot handles by itself gets no mark on the row. The "needs you" mark is a button: with one waiting question it opens that question, otherwise "Asked of me", which lists stuck issues and machine waits with their ways out (#919); the row's menu offers the same as "Open what needs you". A folded group or owner sums its repositories the same way. Hovering the row says, line by line: the repository and its switch; what goes on now, each with its number ("4 workers running · 2 in review"); then each thing that needs you with what to do; then at most one quiet line for the queue ("52 queued", ready and blocked issues together). The screen reader hears the same words. Opening a repository lists up to three lines of current work under it, the running ones first, each with its own mark from the table below. Its filter "Only with open questions or work" keeps the repositories with a question waiting for you, a stuck issue, or a worker running or starting (here or on another machine); blocked, ready, in-review or finished issues and running checks alone do not count (#948). A repository listed twice (under Favourites and in its group) is marked once, in the row it was opened from. Mark Meaning What you do rotating circle Working : a worker is on it right now nothing filled circle with "?" Needs you : a question or an approval answer it on the forge or in Gitoodo; work goes on filled circle with "?" Stuck ( stalled ): the autopilot gave up on it choose a way out on "Asked of me" (see below) filled circle with "?" Stuck on a machine only you can provide choose a way out on "Asked of me" (see below) triangle with "!" Checks fail on the pull request nothing: the worker gets it back to fix them diamond In review : a pull request waits review and merge (or let Gitoodo merge, see settings) circle with a bar Blocked by a dependency or a missing machine nothing: it resolves by itself circle with a dot Claimed by a worker on another machine nothing dashed circle Ready : starts when a worker slot is free nothing check mark Done : a worker just finished nothing Only the two "?" states put a mark on the repository row; the others show in the issue lines under an opened repository, and hovering a line explains it in one sentence. An issue is stuck when its worker made no progress after several restarts, or its checks still fail after the last restart. An issue stalled only because its machine could not start a worker goes back to ready by itself. "Asked of me" lists every stuck issue (#919). A line shows only the reason in a few words and one button, Solve ; it opens the ways out that fit the cause, the recommended one first and marked, each with one quiet line saying what it does: Reason shown Recorded cause Ways out (recommended first) "The worker hung" hung Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "3 runs without a result" no_result Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Checks keep failing" checks_failing Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Merging keeps failing" merge_failed Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Conflicts with the base branch" conflict Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "The branch could not be updated" update_failed Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "The autopilot got no further" no record Solve with an agent, View issue, Pause "Working copy was in use" lease_refused Try again (passing), Solve with an agent, … "The base branch moved faster than the checks ran" base_moving Try again (passing), Solve with an agent, … "The agent waited for a sign-in" login_prompt Try again (after signing in), Solve with an agent, … "The agent waited for a confirmation at its start" trust_prompt see below Try again puts the issue back into the queue ( ready , the stalled label goes). It is offered only where another run can go differently, and says why: the cause was passing (a held working copy, a base branch that moved on), it is gone once the agent is signed in again, or an update fixed it. The only cause an update fixed so far is the confirmation at the agent's start (Claude Code and Codex no longer wait for the folder trust prompt since 2026-11-17): a trust_prompt stall from before that offers "Try again" (an update since fixed it) when this app is newer than the fix; otherwise it gets the ways of the other causes. Every other cause repeats, and another run would only spend tokens. The cause decides, not the recorded transient flag (older records call a hang passing). Solve with an agent opens a session of your own ( docs/agent-session.md , "Solve with an agent") in the issue's worktree, with the issue, the cause and the end of the last run as its first message. The issue keeps stalled meanwhile, so the autopilot never takes it. While the session runs, the line says so and offers "Open session". Once it ended, the line offers **Hand back to the autopilot** in one click ( ready ; the next worker goes on from the branch, and the ended session's tile closes); "Solve" keeps the other ways. Pause the autopilot here takes the issue out of the queue: its status goes and extern comes, and the autopilot no longer touches it. To undo it, remove extern on the forge. It replaces "Put back" and is the one way to dismiss an issue without solving it. View issue opens it in its repository. With two or more stuck issues that may be tried again, Try N again above the list tries exactly those (never the ones whose cause repeats), and its hint names why. After a way out the line goes and every count drops at once, before the next poll shows the change. The dispatcher records the cause in stall.json (state folder) when it gives up. Where the end of the worker's screen or transcript shows a prompt the agent cannot pass alone (the folder trust confirmation, a sign-in), that is the cause. Stalls from before the record existed get their cause read once from the dispatcher log of their last run (a refused merge, failing checks, a held working copy, a hang and the prompt it hung at). A worker that sits silent for 20 seconds at such a prompt ends at once instead of waiting out the hang policy and its restarts. A ready issue is stuck on a machine only you can provide (#919) when it waits for: a host: name no machine answers to: "Run on any fitting machine" (recommended, drops host: ), "Use <machine>" for each fitting machine, "Set up <name>" (opens the worker machine assistant with that name); a named machine with another system than its os: : "Set up a <system> machine" (recommended, the assistant asks for that system), "Run on any machine" (with the warning that it may fail), "Pause the autopilot here"; a machine whose coding agent sign-in expired: "Run on another machine meanwhile" (recommended when another machine fits, drops host: ), "Sign in again" (started here when it is this computer and Claude Code, otherwise the command to type there, with a copy button). The question goes away by itself once the sign-in works again. Each says in one sentence why Gitoodo cannot solve it alone. Waits that end by themselves (a machine offline, at capacity, a usage limit) and issues for a system nobody connected yet stay calm: they are no question (#871, #924). 3. Worker: one agent on one issue State Meaning What happens next Running the agent works in its own worktree it opens a pull request or asks a question Silent no output for a while restarted automatically, a few times at most Stalled still silent after the restarts the issue is marked stalled (see above) Ended the agent exited its result is picked up, the worktree tidied Watching a worker: open its repository. The repository view shows every session running there as a live tile, with the queue (ready issues the autopilot starts next) beside them; fewer sessions get larger tiles. A click opens one tile across the full width and resizes the worker's terminal so the agent draws for it; the terminal fills the view and follows new output (scrolled up, "Jump to latest" goes back). A click into it types straight to the agent, every key including Esc, Tab and Ctrl-C; a click outside or Shift-Esc leaves it (#944). "Maximize" (⌘⇧M, Ctrl+Shift+M) lets the terminal fill the window; the same shortcut, or Esc outside the terminal, restores it. Your own sessions (#991) show there too, apart from the workers ( docs/agent-session.md ). "All repos" → "Sessions" shows the sessions of every repository the same way, with one queue across all of them; the "Terminal" button on the "Issues" page opens the same view. 4. Things Gitoodo repairs on its own An orchestrator that runs for weeks meets crashes, restarts and forge hiccups. These states are not yours to clear: Orphaned issue : labelled in-progress but no worker runs it (the dispatcher stopped, a release failed, a machine vanished). The dispatcher checks every minute and puts such an issue back to ready after about five minutes. "Reset" in "All repos" does it at once. Expired lease : a worker's claim that was not renewed is released, and the issue is queued again. Finished worktrees are removed once their work is merged or saved. Unsaved work of a worker that is gone (uncommitted changes, unpushed commits) is pushed as a backup branch after an hour and its worktree removed, on this machine and on further worker machines (#886). What Gitoodo never does alone is discard work. You can save or discard a leftover earlier in "All repos"; nothing else waits for you. 5. Services The status page answers one question: is everything running? One sentence on top says so in the header's words ("All running", "N need you", "Not running: …"), then one line per part keeps the flow going: app sync, the dispatcher (starts and watches workers), the workers, the background services (the classifier reads forges and sets labels) and the keychain with its tokens.
