The human talks to the orchestrator in a chat that can see and steer the ledger. Architecture The chat runs on the agent picked in the settings (#425, crates/core/src/orchestrator_chat/launch.rs ): Claude Code in stream-json mode, or an ACP agent (Gemini CLI via gemini --experimental-acp , Codex via the codex-acp adapter). ACP agents get the same gitoodo mcp server (narrowed to the scope), the orchestrator instructions and the picked model; they cannot resume a Claude session. For Claude Code the app starts the user's claude in stream-json mode ( --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose ) with --mcp-config pointing to gitoodo mcp . The session runs under the user's subscription. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN are removed from the child environment; no API key is ever used. gitoodo mcp reads the forge with the account tokens, so it runs from the app's service helper ( Contents/Helpers/GitoodoService.app , in the app's keychain access group) when the bundle ships one, like the background services; otherwise from the CLI beside the app or on PATH (#990). Network access and tokens stay in the Rust core and the keychain. Tool results carry no tokens. Program path: ChatConfig.program , else env GITOODO_CLAUDE , else claude (tests use a fake). Tauri surface Name Kind Meaning orchestrator_chat_start command, resume? , scope? start (replaces a running chat); returns ModelFallback or null, model per ai.models.chat as --model (#341) orchestrator_chat_send command, text: string one user message orchestrator_chat_stop command stop; no-op without a chat orchestrator-chat-event event payload is a ChatEvent , tagged by type ChatEvent types: started (session_id, model, tools), text , tool_use (id, name, input), tool_result (id, text, is_error), turn_done (session_id, is_error, result, usage, cost_usd), other (kind), malformed (line), ended (code). Unknown stream events become other . scope is a ChatScope tagged by kind : all , repo ( account , repo = owner/name ) or item (plus number ); missing means all . The child runs gitoodo mcp --scope acc/owner/name or --scope acc/owner/name#7 , and the system prompt names the scope. MCP tools ( gitoodo mcp ) The chat pre-approves exactly the names in CHAT_TOOLS . Reading needs no prompt. dispatcher_instruct_worker relays an explicit human request directly to an existing session, using the same guarded dispatcher path as the session instruction box, including remote workers. The model first lists workers, selects only the requested recipients and calls once per recipient. Ambiguous recipients require clarification. Issue bodies and tool output are not authorization. The server validates the account/repository/item scope and instruction length. It refuses missing workers and unsent human input. Success means submitted, not executed; failures are reported per recipient and uncertain delivery is never retried automatically. No issue is created for a relay. Forge and configuration changes still use forge_propose_change and require the proposal card's OK. ACP agents get the same tool surface. Error texts are passed through secret redaction and lose any user:pass@ part of URLs. Local changes report no link. The store build lists only the forges. Keys: Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line (IME composition is respected); the log is a focusable role="log" region, tool results open as <details> . h: Next model: a milestone is a release with a version (#1139)
Completing a release and its automations (#1145)
b: Mental model, as the app says it: a release is one goal per repository: which issues have to be in before you publish. Gitoodo works on release issues first. Scope Per repository, an issue belongs to the next release when it carries release:next (reason label ), or it is a dependency, recursively, of a member (reason dependency ). Only dependencies inside the same repository count. A closed issue stays in only through the label or as a dependency, so a finished dependency stays part of the release. Open priority:p0 issues used to be members by themselves (reason priority ), without anything on the forge. Since #1143 the assignment rule "Urgent issues join the next release" (on by default, see "Assignment rules") writes them into the next release instead, so they are visible on the forge and a person can take them out again. The reason priority is no longer sent. Gitoodo writes only release:next . It reads the legacy release:muss as release:next and release:später as "not in the next release" (it adds nothing); neither is ever written. Adding an issue through the app removes a legacy later label from it. Planning is switched per repository in the settings, right beside the repository's activation ("Release planning", default on; stored as releases in the repository options). With it off, the repository has no scope, no bonus and does not appear in the views. Labels and milestones Today the label is the source of truth: it works the same on every forge, needs no setup and is what the classifier already reads. A milestone only names the release and gives it a due date; the existing milestone rule keeps members in the planned milestone. Next model: a milestone is a release with a version (#1139) Release management (epic #1139) moves to this model: **a milestone whose title is a version is a release**, and release:next stays as "the next release, version not decided yet". Other milestones (sprints, themes) stay the user's own and are never treated as releases. Step 1 (#1140) adds the forge calls in the Rust core only; nothing of it is visible in the app yet , and the planning, scope and closing described here are unchanged until the later steps switch over. A milestone title counts as a release version ( forge::release::release_version ) when, after trimming, it is optionally v / V directly before the number, or one of the words version , release , build , ver (any case) followed by a space, - or _ , then one to four numbers separated by dots (each at most nine digits), then optionally a pre-release or build part after - or + of letters, digits, dots and hyphens ( -rc.1 , +20261119 ), allowed only after a dotted number or a prefix word, and nothing else. So v1.2.3 , 1.2 , 2026.11 , 42 , build 42 , Release 1.4 and 1.0.0-rc.1 are releases; Sprint 12 , Q4 2026 , Milestone 3 , v1.2 Winter , 1.x , 1.2.3.4.5 , 12-sprint and 2026-11-19 are not. Forge calls (core only) Forgejo/Gitea GitHub GitLab Milestones: list, create, edit, close, reopen milestones ( state ) milestones ( state , by number) milestones ( state_event ) Issues of a milestone issues?milestones=<title> issues?milestone=<number> issues?milestone=<title> Assign/unassign an issue milestone (0 clears) milestone (null clears) milestone_id (0 clears) Tag on a commit tags git/tags (annotated) + git/refs repository/tags Release: create, read, edit releases (drafts) releases (drafts) releases , no drafts Right for tags and releases write:repository + write access Contents: Read and write ( repo ) + write access api + at least Developer Rules that hold on every forge: Creating a tag is idempotent: the same tag on the same commit is success, on another commit it is refused and the tag is never moved or deleted. A release is created as a draft where the forge has drafts. An existing draft is reused (name and notes updated, it stays a draft); a published release is left as it is and only changed on an explicit call. GitLab has no drafts: a draft request is refused before anything is sent, and a GitLab release is public as soon as it exists. GitLab group milestones can be read and assigned, but not edited or closed through the project; the error says to change them in the group's milestones or to use a project milestone. Gitoodo never edits a group milestone, because that would change other repositories too. Every write goes through the audit log ( milestone_create , milestone_edit , tag_create , release_create , release_edit ). Refusals (403, 404, 405, 409, 422) name the missing right or the cause and never contain the token. The release rights ( rights::check_release ) are checked separately from the mode check, so they do not appear as missing in the app yet. Known limits of step 1: a due date can be set or changed but not cleared; tag protection rules (GitHub rulesets, Forgejo/Gitea tag protection, GitLab protected tags) are not read in advance, so a protected tag shows up as a refusal when it is created; GitLab has no pre-release flag. Version logic and suggestion (#1142) Step 3 of #1139 adds the version rules in the Rust core ( orchestration::version ). There is no screen for them yet; the settings come with the repository settings page (#926). Config. Each repository can have a version entry in its rule in orchestration.json in the app's config folder. It is never stored in the repository. Without the entry the repository uses SemVer with every preset. { "scheme": { "kind": "semver" }, "raises": [{ "source": "label", "name": "api-change", "part": "major" }], "presets": ["plain", "prefixed", "issue_types"], "default_part": "patch" } scheme.kind Version semver v1.4.2 calendar pattern from YYYY , YY , MM , M , DD , D and the counter N : YYYY.MM , YYYY.MM.N build one rising number: 42 , build 42 pattern text around {major} , {minor} , {patch} or {n} : v{major}.{minor}.{patch} , release-{major}.{minor} , build-{n} script command runs in the local checkout and prints the version A pattern is refused when it cannot be read back as a version: a field twice or two fields without text between them, digits in the text, a calendar without year or month, the counter not last, {n} mixed with the other fields, fields out of order, or a result that is no release title ( b{n} gives b0 , which is not a version; build-{n} is). Patterns and commands are limited to 1000 characters, own rules to 200. version_config_validate lists the problems with field, code and text. Raise of an issue. Each label ( source: label ) and the native issue type ( source: type ) is looked up, case-insensitive: first the repository's own raises , then the presets. An own rule replaces the preset for that name. The issue raises the highest part found; an issue that no rule matches raises default_part . Native types are GitHub's organisation issue types ( type.name ) and GitLab's issue_type ( issue , incident , task ); Forgejo/Gitea have none and use labels only. The prefixed preset takes the plain words after type: , type:: , type/ , typ: , kind/ or kind: ( type::feature , kind/bug ). Preset major minor patch plain breaking , breaking-change feature , enhancement bug , fix , bugfix , security prefixed type:breaking , … type::feature , … kind/bug , … issue_types Breaking , Breaking change Feature , Enhancement Bug , Incident Suggestion. The release's issues are the issues of the next release milestone (see "Queue order") plus the release scope, open or closed. The highest raise among them is applied to the last released version. The reason names the issues at that raise: "minor because of #12, #15" (the first ten, then "and N more"), or "patch, no issue asks for more". The last released version is the highest version that fits the scheme among the closed release milestones and the tags. Neither source wins by kind; the higher version wins, so a tag made without a milestone counts as much as a milestone closed without a tag. On a tie the milestone's spelling is kept and the origin is both . Pre-release versions ( 1.3.0-rc.1 ) never count, build metadata ( +… ) is ignored. If the forge refuses the tags, the milestones alone are used and tags_read is false . Before 1.0 (SemVer and patterns with major and minor) a breaking change raises the minor part ( 0.4.2 → 0.5.0 ). 1.0.0 is never suggested; the user sets it by changing the suggestion. A part the pattern does not have raises the lowest part it has ( release-{major}.{minor} : a patch raises the minor part). Without a previous version: SemVer v0.1.0 , a pattern with major and minor 0.1.0 in its form, a major-only pattern, {n} and build give 1 , calendar gives today's period with counter 0. Calendar ignores the raise: today's period (UTC) with counter 0, or the next counter while the last version is in the same period. Without a counter, a second release in one period is an error, as is a last version later than today. Own script. The script runs only in the user's local checkout of the repository (a plain clone outside the worktree root, never a worktree), through the same runner as the automations' prechecks ( automations::command ): environment cleared down to the automations' allow-list, so no token is passed, stdin closed, 60 s timeout, at most 64 KiB of stdout and of stderr each. Inputs: Variable Value GITOODO_LAST_VERSION the last released version, empty without one GITOODO_RELEASE_ISSUES path of a JSON temp file with the release's issues, removed afterwards GITOODO_VERSION_RAISE major , minor or patch GITOODO_REPO owner/name Its stdout must be exactly one line (one trailing line break allowed) that is a release title of at most 100 characters. Anything else (exit code not 0, a timeout, too much output, no line, several lines, no version) is an error that shows stdout and stderr; it never becomes a version. The hygiene and the MCP tool never run the script: the hygiene skips the milestone question with a notice, the MCP tool answers that the app or the CLI runs it. Naming the next milestone. The hygiene's question to create the next release milestone proposes the suggestion's version (it used to count up the last number of the newest milestone). Surfaces. Read only, no UI yet: Tauri: version_suggest(account, repo) ( outcome : suggested with the suggestion, or failed with the failure), version_config(account, repo) , version_config_validate(config) and set_version_config(account, repo, config | null) ( saved or invalid with the problems). CLI: gitoodo release-version --repo owner/name [--account id] [--json] [--check] , for example v1.5.0 (minor because of #11, #13; last v1.4.2 from a closed milestone) . --check only checks the stored config. MCP tool ledger_version_suggestion (optional repo ). Assignment rules (#1143) Each repository has a list of assignment rules in the app's orchestration config ( orchestration.json , release_rules in the repository's entry; never in the repository). The rules decide which issues join which release by themselves. No view uses them yet ; the rules come with the release settings on the repository settings page. A rule ( orchestration::assignment::AssignmentRule ) has an id (unique in the list) and a name , enabled (default on); conditions over the issue and combine : all (default) or any . Attributes: attribute condition label carries the label value (any case; the catalog's name is resolved per repo) state open or closed author opened by the login value (any case, @ optional) origin follow_up (body names "Follow-up of #n"/"Folge von #n") or follow_up_in_release (the parent is in an open release milestone or carries release:next ) age days since it was opened, at_least and/or at_most priority the priority label's level: value p0 … p3 , or at_least / at_most as numbers issue_type the forge's native issue type value (GitHub types, GitLab issue/incident/task) a target : {"kind":"next"} (the next release: its milestone when one with a version is open, else release:next ), {"kind":"parent"} (the release of the issue's parent; used with origin ) or {"kind":"named","title":"v2.0"} (an open

Every open issue in the overview has exactly one status. Code: crates/core/src/status.rs . Statuses and recommended labels Status Standard label Derived when open status/open nothing else applies in_progress status/in-progress the issue has an assignee in_review status/in-review an open pull request closes it ( Closes #N ) blocked status/blocked never derived, label only needs_user status/needs-you an open question to the user exists Standard labels match case-insensitively. Precedence Label mapping of the account (label name to status). Standard labels from the table. Derivation from forge data, checked in this order: open question to the user, linked open pull request, assignee, otherwise open . If several labels of one tier match, the most urgent status wins ( blocked , needs_user , in_review , in_progress , open ), so the label order never matters. Derivation works on the data every adapter already reports (Forgejo/Gitea, GitHub, GitLab). Mapping Stored in settings.json as status_mapping : account id to an object {"<label>": "<status>"} . It is part of the settings backup ( docs/settings-backup.md ); files without the key load unchanged. Mappings of removed accounts are dropped on load, label names are trimmed and compared case-insensitively. Stale threshold Stored as stale : {"days": 3, "repos": {"<account id>": {"<owner/repo>": <days>}}} . An open issue without activity for days counts as stale; a repo entry overrides the global value. 0 or a missing key means the default (3 days), values are capped at 365, overrides of removed accounts are dropped. Settings page Settings, group "Work", row "Overview" ( settings-leitstand ) opens the page settings-leitstand-page : Stale: the global value ( settings-leitstand-stale-days-input ), then per account a list of the account's repos ( settings-leitstand-repos-<account> ); each repo has a days field (blank = same as all repos) and a reset button ( …-reset , disabled without an own value). Labels per account ( settings-leitstand-mapping-<account>-<status>-input ): your own labels per status, comma separated, with the recommended standard label shown below. A label entered for one status moves away from another, so it never stands for two. Fields save on blur or Enter through save_settings . Changes apply without a restart: when the mapping or the stale settings change, save_settings marks the cached overview data outdated, and the restarted account loops fetch it again on their next poll instead of after five minutes. For the UI RepoCounts.issues (dashboard rows) lists the open issues per repo with status.status and status.source ( mapping , standard_label , derived ).

Every counter in Gitoodo shows a value of one Counts value, computed in Rust ( crates/core/src/sync/counts.rs , SyncHub::counts in src-tauri/src/sync.rs ). The webview never counts on its own; it reads get_counts once and follows the counts event. Counter Value Tray title and tooltip total Tab "Fragen", header total + refused merges + status Heading "Fragen" questions , tasks , approvals Bundle "Freigabe" open approvals (#705) total = questions + tasks + approvals , so the single tab shows the tray number. Approvals of foreign contributions ( intake-approval-* cards) are no questions: the heading counts them apart, and the bundle above the list holds them. Tasks for the human are waiting items without a valid open question block ( needs-human with a description and maybe a - [ ] acceptance list, e.g. a step in a developer portal only a person can do; crates/core/src/human_task.rs ). They ask for a hands-on step, not a decision: the list shows them in their repo's group after its questions with the tag "Aufgabe" (#897), the sheet as "Aufgabe" with the checklist, "Erledigt" and "Zurück an den Orchestrator" (both with an optional note "Anmerkung (optional)"; on a hand-back the note is the person's instruction to the worker, see "Instructions" in docs/question-format.md ), and the heading names every kind that waits ("6 Fragen · 3 Aufgaben · 161 Freigaben"; only questions: "6 Fragen warten auf dich"). There is no inbox of forge notifications any more (#189): Gitoodo never fetches or marks forge notifications, and only waiting items are counted. The header shows no count (#84): each number appears once, on its tab. One "needs you" (#919). The header's overall state ("3 need you"), the badge on "Fragen an mich" and what that page lists on landing are one set, and a click on the header's number always lands on that page while the number is above zero: total (questions, tasks and approvals in scope, see "Autopilot scope" below), issues the autopilot gave up on ("Hängt fest", label stalled ) in repos with the autopilot on, listed on the page with their reason and "Try again", "Put back" and "View issue" (#919, see docs/states.md ). They are no approvals any more: a worker ran on them, so the issue never reads "waits for your approval" ( intake::reason ), ready issues in repos with the autopilot on that wait for a machine only the user can provide (an unknown host: , a machine with the wrong system, an expired agent sign-in), one each, listed on the page with their ways out ( repoNeeds(…).hosts , #919). The status part "workers" no longer counts these ( statusWaitCount ), so nothing counts twice, merges a repository setting refuses and the user still has to fix ( waitingBlocks , #942), the parts of the status only the user can fix ( countedParts : a rejected sign-in, a keychain approval, ready issues waiting for a worker machine, a service that does not answer, …), each shown as a card with its fixing action at the top of the page. A disk running low is left out (#970): it has its own entry in the status bar, its own notification and its problem on the status page. The repo part (questions in scope that are not answered yet, plus stalled issues and machine waits only the user can resolve in scope, repoNeedsCount ) comes from one place, repoNeeds over the sidebar's activity ( src/views/sidebar/repoActivity.ts ): the repos' marks ("3 issues need you") add up to it, and the header, the badge and the page use it, so the header always equals the sum of the repos' marks plus refused merges plus status problems, which have no repo mark. needsYouTotal in src/views/shell/overall.ts adds them up; landing in src/views/questions/landing.ts is what the page lists, and needsYouCount.test.ts pins both to each other for a mix of questions, tasks, approvals, refused merges, machine notices, stalled issues, machine waits and repos with and without the autopilot. A way out taken on the page takes its issue out of every count at once ( markResolved in useRepoWorkspace.ts , for at most five minutes until the read model shows the change). Repos without the autopilot never feed the number : their questions, tasks and approvals wait behind the page's quiet "N more from repos without autopilot – show" at the end, and that N is never added anywhere. The tray title shows only total : refused merges and status problems have their own notifications there. Tray and webview are updated from the same Counts in the same call ( publish_counts ), after every poll, after answering or commenting, and after removing an account. Rule Questions : open entries of all "waiting for me" views that count in the tray, over all accounts, minus questions answered through the app (answer card or free comment) whose waiting_since is not newer than the posted comment. Such an answer is dropped at the next poll once the question has left the list or waits again. The popover shows the same questions teal ("handled"). Kind ( account_counts , mirrored by waitKind in src/views/questions/tasks.ts ): an entry whose newest card is an intake approval is an approval; one without an open question block is a task; every other entry is a question. Each entry counts once. Overview (#237, #933), the start page: statistics only. It lists no questions and shows no "needs you" number; that number lives in the header and on "Fragen an mich". Repo rows with an open question (same rule) carry a mark without a number. No sidebar filter changes that number. Disabled repos (#135): items of repos switched off in the settings are in no list, no counter, no unseen mark and no system notification. They are dropped centrally ( without_disabled , read by SyncHub::tally and the snapshot events), so switching a repo off updates tray and lists at once; switching it on shows its items again (after the next sync for what the poll skipped). Ungated repos (#705): approvals of repos this app's orchestrator lists as observed or paused are in no counter and no list ( without_ungated , from Config::ungated ), since nothing works on them there; the paused intake asks no new ones. Repos it does not list keep their approvals. The other questions of those repos count as before. Autopilot scope (#897): in the orchestrator mode only repos with the autopilot on ( active in orchestration.json , Config::autopilot ) count. What waits in paused, observed or unlisted repos is in no counter, no unseen mark, no reminder, no chat notice and no system notification ( within_autopilot in SyncHub::tally and SyncHub::counted , within_scope for the toasts); the sidebar sets no "needs you" mark there either. The snapshot event names the repos ( autopilot ), so "Fragen an mich" lists those first, grouped by repo with the questions before the tasks, and keeps the rest behind "N weitere aus Repos ohne Autopilot – anzeigen" at the end. The direct mode and the setting asked_all_repos ("Fragen auch aus Repos ohne Autopilot", Settings → Notifications) count every repo ( autopilot is null ). Switching a repo's autopilot or the setting republishes counts and snapshots at once; an unreadable orchestration file hides nothing. List filters (search, repo, kind, status; #61) never change any counter. They narrow what a list shows, not what waits; otherwise the tray (which knows no filters) and the popover would disagree. Under an active filter only the head of the view says "shown of total" (e.g. "3 of 12 questions need you", #109); without a filter it shows the total. A failing account keeps its last good entries, so its counts stay stable until the next successful poll. Paging: every list request follows the forge's Link header ( collect_pages ), so counts are not capped at one page of 50. Seen and unseen Every counted item (open question) is either seen or unseen ( crates/core/src/store/viewed.rs , unseen_keys in counts.rs ). Seen means the item was visible in the opened list: its row stayed at least 60 % in view for about 0.7 s while the window was focused and visible. The webview only reports the keys ( mark_seen ); Rust looks up the item's activity time and stores it as the mark. New activity makes it unseen again : a question whose waiting_since is newer than its mark is unseen. Answered (handled) questions are never unseen. Snooze ( snooze_question , unsnooze_question ): a snoozed question leaves the list, the counters and the unseen marks until its wake-up time (presets: 1 hour, tomorrow 09:00 local, 1 week; computed in src/state/snooze.ts ). It returns by itself at that time (timer plus every poll), without restart. New activity on the issue does not wake it early. Stored per account in viewed.json ( snoozed , unix seconds); expired or vanished entries are pruned on the next poll. Tray : one unseen item turns the tray check red (macOS and Windows); the tooltip names how many, e.g. "Gitoodo (3, 1 unseen)". Counts.unseen carries the number. Lists : unseen rows carry a small neutral ink dot (6 px) and a hidden "Neu"/"New" for screen readers, never red. A dot stays while the user looks at the list and is gone once the window loses focus, so it never vanishes under the user's eyes. Persistence : marks live in viewed.json next to the settings and survive restarts. Marks of items that left the lists are dropped at the next poll; a removed account is forgotten. Local only : viewed.json is not part of the settings export and is never sent anywhere. System notifications A system notification appears only for a new hit of a "waiting for me" view that counts in the tray (assignment and labels as set in the criteria editor, #143). A plain new issue that no counting view matches never notifies, neither does a hit in a view that does not count, and an item in two counting views notifies exactly once (the hits are de-duplicated by repo and number in fetch_account ). The first poll after a start is the baseline and notifies nothing. Covered by the tests in crates/core/src/sync/fetch.rs . Where a click leads (#939) Every notification carries its target, and a click brings the app forward and opens it there: Notification Opens New question (poll, dispatcher, reminder) the question's card over "Asked of me" Several new questions (summary) "Asked of me" Worker stalled, merge failed, merge vetoed the issue or pull request on its repository's page Issue waits for its worker machine Settings → Worker machines Invalid orchestrator settings the status page Low disk space (#970) Settings → Storage Usage limit warning nothing beyond the app (no single place to open) The target holds only kind, account id, owner/name and number, never a token. The core keeps the last clicked target until the window takes it ( take_notification_target ) and announces it with the event notification-open , so a window that opens only because of the click still finds it. Per platform: macOS: the target travels in the request identifier of the UNNotificationRequest ; a delegate of UNUserNotificationCenter reports the click ( crates/scoped-folder/src/notification.rs ), also when the click started the app. Windows MSIX (store build or installed package): the toast's launch arguments carry the target; its Activated handler reports a click while the app runs. A click after the app ended starts it without the target (no toast activator is registered). Direct Windows install and Linux: the notification plugin reports no click, so a click only brings the app forward, as the system does by itself. Every alert of the dispatcher is worded in the app language (title and body); a question names its first line, else the issue title, never the dispatcher's log text. On a question alert the app reads that one issue again at once ( fetch_issue , the same filters as the full poll) and posts the notification only once the list has the question, or after 5 s at the latest; the poll that later finds the same question does not announce it a second time. Covered by the tests in src-tauri/src/human_control.rs , src-tauri/src/notify_target.rs , src-tauri/src/sync.rs an

t: Start: first paint and loading state
h: What the window shows while loading
b: The window is never empty after a start. It shows the last known state at once and replaces it part by part as the accounts and repositories answer. "Synced" only shows once every account has answered. Where the window opens The window opens on the start page: the statistics overview ( src/views/overview/OverviewView.tsx , docs/metrics.md , "Overview dashboard"), with what only the user can fix above the figures. The way back to it from anywhere is the first entry of the navigation, "Überblick" ("Overview", key 1), marked like every entry while the start page shows. The header shows the same full wordmark on every view, never a view title (each view names itself in its own heading), so the top of the window does not change when a repository or a page opens. The wordmark is a second way to the start page: a button named "Gitoodo, zum Überblick" ("Gitoodo, go to the overview"), reachable with Tab and pressed with Enter or Space. The introduction tour points at the navigation entry. What the next start opens ( src/state/lastView.ts , kept in the window's local storage, never in start-view.json ): Before the window closed Next start Nothing kept (first start, private mode, damaged entry) The start page. The start page, a tab ("All repos", "Asked of me", Chat) The start page. A repository's page, or a question or the settings opened on it That repository's page; Back leads to the start page. A repository that is gone since The start page. The onboarding handed over to the setup assistant The setup assistant over the start page. Why not the tab of earlier: the start page answers "is everything running?" in one look, which is the question at every start, and a list from earlier can have changed meanwhile. A repository is the exception: whoever closed the window inside one was in the middle of its work. "All repos" keeps its subpage, so the tab shows the page used last. A kept "Overview" subpage of earlier versions opens the start page. The view from earlier What is stored: a compact copy of what the window showed: the accounts (id, kind, label, address, login), each account's last good snapshot (questions and tasks, dashboard rows, repo list), the orchestrator's repositories (state and issues) and the counts. Errors are not stored; they belong to the moment. Where it lives: start-view.json in the app's state folder (the folder that also holds settings.json ). It is local only: it is not part of the settings export, and it is never sent anywhere. Who writes it: the window composes the view ( src/state/startView.ts ). The core stores it ( crates/core/src/store/start_view.rs ): fields whose names suggest a secret ( token , password , secret , cookie , credential , authorization , api_key , private_key , auth ) are dropped; every text passes the log redaction: registered tokens, token prefixes and URL credentials are replaced; the file stays under 4 MiB. A bigger view first loses issue bodies and comments, and a view that is still too big is not stored at all. When it is written: at most every 3 seconds while the window shows data that arrived since the start. The view from earlier alone is never stored again. Version: a view with another version, or a damaged one, is ignored whole, never shown in part. The next save replaces it. What the window shows while loading Part Not known yet From earlier Sidebar Shimmering placeholder rows; at the foot while an account's repositories are not listed Rows as before; "From earlier" next to the heading (the hover gives the time); "from earlier" in the row's tooltip Repository row A short shimmering bar where its state will show; "loading" in its label and tooltip Its last state Group or owner No count, and a placeholder instead of "Empty. Drag repositories here…" Its count from earlier Questions The skeleton; once some arrived, shimmering rows under the list The questions from earlier; "From earlier" behind the heading Counters An empty shimmering pill, never "0" The counts from earlier Status bar "Loading repositories …", or "Loading 12 of 34 repositories …" once the totals are known Same Rules: Synced: "Synced" (with its age) only shows once every account that the core polls has answered at least once since the start. A failed poll is also an answer; the error bar says why it failed. Until then the status bar counts the repositories that have answered. Unknown is not zero: a repository whose data has not arrived is a placeholder, never missing, "Empty" or a count of 0. "Only with work" keeps such repositories in the list until their data is known. A failed first poll keeps the data from earlier, still marked as from earlier. Repository by repository: the core reports each repository's progress as it is fetched (the repo-progress event: the account's listing first, then for each repository the start of each read and one event once it is through, with its dashboard row). The sidebar and the counts fill in as the events arrive, without waiting for the whole account. The start panel While the content shows nothing but placeholders (the first-sync skeleton of "Asked of me" or the issues list), a card in the middle of the content says what loads right now ( src/views/shell/LoadPanel.tsx , model in src/state/loadPanel.ts ): a title, a bar with "12 of 32" (without a value while a repo list is still open), the current step in plain words ("Reading issues and pull requests of owner/name and 3 more …"), and the four phases: accounts, lists, issues and pull requests, questions; a repo whose read takes 5 seconds or more is named as slow; a repo or an account that failed is named once, with the note that loading goes on with the others. It never blocks: it lies over the content only, takes no pointer or focus, and the sidebar and header stay usable. It shows only after 400 ms (a fast start never flashes), fades out once the first useful view is there and never comes back in this window: later refreshes only use the status bar. A start with a view from earlier shows that view at once, so the card appears only where the view from earlier has nothing to show. Screen readers hear the progress at most every 5 seconds; reduced motion drops the fade and the running band. The core reports the reads as part of repo-progress : reading (with pass : questions or issues ) when a pass starts a repo, and failed on a repo that could not be read. Names only. The browser demo adds a slow and a failed repo with ?stagger&trouble . Shimmer Placeholders use the shared .shimmer class ( src/ui/tokens.css ): the grey --color-skeleton with a light band ( --color-skeleton-shine ) that runs across it every 1.8 seconds. With reduced motion the band is off, and the placeholder only fades slowly. It uses design tokens only, never a meaning colour. Measuring The window logs its start once, when every account has answered, as the start_timings event ( docs/logging.md ). It records milliseconds since the page began loading: firstContentMs : first content shows, either from earlier or from the core; sidebarMs : the sidebar names every repository with data, with no placeholder left; allLoadedMs : every account has answered; plus the number of accounts and repositories, and whether a view from earlier was shown. The values are also on globalThis.gitoodoStartTimings while the window runs. The browser demo simulates a slow start with ?stagger (or ?stagger=<ms> , the base step, default 400). It works like this: every account starts unsynced; each account lists its repositories after one to four steps, reports them one by one at its own pace and then sends its full snapshot; the orchestrator answers after two steps; the demo keeps its view from earlier for the tab, so a reload shows the second start. Measured in the demo (4 accounts, 60 repositories, ?stagger=400 , Vite dev server, headless Chrome): Start First content Sidebar complete All loaded First (nothing earlier) 481 ms 9605 ms 10115 ms Again (view from earlier) 139 ms 139 ms 9797 ms In both starts, placeholders show from the first frame. On the second start, the sidebar shows all 60 repositories from earlier at once.

Gitoodo writes a structured log to help explain what happened on a user's machine (for example a token check that failed, a worker that did not start, or a sync that keeps failing). The app and every background service (classifier, dispatcher with its worker supervision, satellite) use the same module ( crates/core/src/logging ) and schema. The log never contains tokens, Authorization headers, response bodies, or URL paths and queries; servers are logged as host[:port] only. Location One folder per user, shared by the app and the services: System Folder macOS ~/Library/Logs/de.gitoodo.app/ Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\de.gitoodo.app\logs\ Linux $XDG_STATE_HOME/gitoodo/logs/ ( ~/.local/state/... ) GITOODO_LOG_DIR overrides the folder; with GITOODO_STATE_DIR set (tests, isolated runs) it is <state>/logs . The test-access build keeps its own folder under its identifier. File Writer gitoodo.log the app classifier.jsonl gitoodo classifier (also when the app starts it) dispatcher.jsonl gitoodo dispatcher , including the workers it supervises satellite.jsonl gitoodo satellite (not the --stdio bridge) <service>.stderr.log stderr of a service (bootstrap errors, a crash before logging started) runs/<run_id>/… terminal transcript of one worker run (see Worker transcripts ) Each process owns its file through a sidecar lock ( <file>.lock ). A second process of the same kind (for example a classifier service waiting for the app's classifier) writes <name>-<pid>.<ext> instead, so two processes never rotate one file. Each line is one JSON object (schema v 2): { "v": 2, "ts": "2026-11-16T11:00:11.175Z", "seq": 12, "level": "warn", "proc": "dispatcher", "pid": 4711, "component": "dispatch", "event": "dispatch.host_wait", "cid": null, "run_id": null, "issue": "owner/repo#42", "span": null, "audit": false, "msg": "waiting for a host; no matching host can take it", "ctx": { "host": "mac-mini", "reason": "offline" } } ts : UTC, RFC 3339 with milliseconds. seq : line number within the process, so gaps show dropped lines. proc : app , classifier , dispatcher or satellite ; pid the process ID. event : stable name; service events are dotted ( <area>.<what> ), app events keep their earlier names. msg is human text, never parsed. cid is a correlation ID: every line of one sync run (or one command) shares it. A cid field on an event (a classifier decision the dispatcher refers to) is lifted out of ctx . run_id , issue and span are top-level for every line ( null when unknown): a field of that name on an event is lifted out of ctx . run_id and span are reserved for timed worker runs (see Runs and steps ). ctx holds the remaining typed fields (at most 32), each redacted. Levels Level Meaning error Unrecoverable failure the user relies on (token check failed, keychain write failed) warn Failed, but retried or carried on (sync failed, integration error, keychain read failed) info State changes (sync finished, settings changed, audit events) debug Detail (sync started, every keychain access) Dependencies log only warn and error . Rotation, budget and retention Per file: 5 MiB, then the file becomes <file>.1 (older generations shift, beyond .3 they are deleted): at most 4 files and 20 MiB per process. A line that would not fit after a failed rotation is dropped rather than written past the cap (on Windows a file held open by a viewer cannot be renamed; Gitoodo then copies and empties it, and if that fails too it drops lines and retries after 30 s). The next written line reports the count as dropped_line . Whole folder: a disk budget, default 75 MiB (setting log_budget_mb , 20–500), covering every log and stderr file in the folder and one level of subfolders. Files older than 14 days (setting log_max_age_days , 1–90) are deleted. When the folder is over budget, the oldest files that no running process writes are deleted first. *.stderr.log files are emptied above 1 MiB. When: at the start of every process and every 6 h after ( log.cleanup names what was removed). Files of a running process are never deleted; their size is bounded by the per-file cap. gitoodo diagnose shows the folder's size against the budget. Service events Area Events every service service.started ( version ), service.stopped , service.fatal ( error ), panic ( location ), log.cleanup classifier (polls) classifier.cycle ( duration_ms , accounts , repos , errors , forge_requests , forge_cached , forge_not_modified , forge_failures , forge_not_found , forge_rate_limited , forge_retry_wait_ms , forge_p50_ms , forge_p95_ms , forge_max_ms ) after every poll dispatcher (forge) dispatch.forge_summary (the same forge_* fields) every 5 min when it made requests forge requests (every process) forge.request_failed (warn; a 404 at debug) and forge.request_recovered (info), see Forge requests dispatcher (control) control.received ( cmd , action , issue ), control.applied ( result , duration_ms , error ): park, stop, restart, attach and worker requests at info, queries at debug; never texts or capabilities workers worker.transcript ( path ), worker.transcript_failed , worker.transcripts_recovered ( count ) classifier classifier.started , .lock_wait , .lock_taken , .handover , .parent_gone , .poll_error , .account_error , .reconciled classifier (runs) classifier.ready ( cid , issue , previous ): an issue became ready; classifier.ready_seen ( count , repos ): issues already ready when the classifier first saw them (start, repo switched on), whose single classifier.ready lines ( previous: unseen ) are debug dispatcher dispatch.started , .worker_started , .worker_exit , .start_failed , .host_wait ( issue , reason , since , detail ), .wait ( reason , since ), .hung , .merged , .merge_failed , .lease_* , .cleanup , .shutdown dispatcher (machine faults) see Machine faults runs run.start , run.end , span.start , span.end , satellite.clock (see below) automations (in dispatcher) automation.started , .postponed , .rate_limited , .gave_up , .config_error , .retired ( jobs : switched off once because they worked the queue, #953) satellite satellite.listening , .worker_started , .worker_exit ( run_id , code , duration_ms ), .spawn_failed , .kill , .delivery_failed , .subscription_lost , .shutdown ; worker hooks ( issue ): .worker_nudged , .worker_idle , .worker_finished ( run_id ), .worker_continued Fields used across events: issue (issue key), host , repo , error (redacted text), reason . Forge requests Every failed attempt of a forge request is one forge.request_failed line at warn: host (host[:port]), method , endpoint (the API route with every name, number and query replaced by * , for example /api/v1/repos/*/*/issues/*/comments ; never the path or the query), repo ( owner/name , when the route names one), status (HTTP, if any), kind (the token check categories below), attempt (1-based), outcome ( retrying , gave_up or not_retried ), retry_in_ms and repeats . Lines with the same host, method, endpoint and kind are throttled like other errors (see Throttling ). A request that succeeds after failed attempts logs forge.request_recovered ( attempts ). A 404 is an answer the callers handle (a deleted issue, an optional route), so it is logged at debug and counted in forge_not_found , not in forge_failures . The forge_* fields count, since the last summary: forge_requests sent, forge_cached reads answered without a request, forge_not_modified conditional reads the forge answered with 304, forge_failures failed attempts (rate limits included), forge_not_found 404 answers, and the retry wait and latency percentiles. A classifier poll reads each forge route once per account: inside the poll, repeated GETs (the reconcile pass, the queue snapshot and the read model read the same listings) are answered from memory, and a write to a repo makes the poll read that repo again. Replies with an ETag (GitHub, GitLab) are kept across polls and asked with If-None-Match . Forgejo and Gitea send no ETag ; there the comments of an issue whose updated_at and comment count did not change are reused for up to 10 minutes. The cache lives in process memory only, keyed by a fingerprint of the credential, never by the token itself. Logs name the API family neutrally: gitea-compatible covers Forgejo and Gitea, which share the API and are not told apart without a signed-in request. Runs and steps One attempt of the dispatcher at an issue is a run with its own ID, r- and 10 lowercase Crockford base32 characters ( r-7k2m9q4xzt ). Every line of the attempt carries it in run_id , whichever process writes it: The classifier logs classifier.ready with a fresh cid when an issue becomes ready and keeps that decision ( cid , since when) in the read model while the issue stays ready. Issues that are ready when first seen get their decision too, but their lines are debug and one classifier.ready_seen line counts them. The dispatcher creates the run ID when it picks the issue up and logs run.start with that cid , host , worker and agent , so the run is linked to the decision. The ID is stored in the worktree lease, sent to a satellite in the spawn request and given to the worker as GITOODO_RUN_ID . Satellite lines of the worker (its worktree, spawn and satellite.worker_exit ) carry it, and so does the main host's delivery ( pr.open ) of a satellite branch. The pull request itself does not carry it. run.end closes the run with duration_ms and result : merged , stalled , needs_human , parked , paused , user_stop , start_failed , lease_refused , host_gone or skipped . Each step is a span. A step that runs within one call is logged as span.start and span.end ; a step that already happened ( queue.wait , host.select , merge ) as one span.end . span.end always has duration_ms and result ( ok , error , cancelled , timeout ); otherwise also error_kind and, where useful, error (redacted). A run that ends with steps still open ends them with the run's outcome. Step From → to Error kinds queue.wait the classifier's ready decision → the dispatcher's pickup ( since ) – host.select choosing the host among the ready issues of the repo – clone.ensure finding the working copy, cloning it when missing, fetching the base (local hosts); sending the copy to a worker machine clone_failed worktree.create cutting the worktree (on the dispatcher or the satellite) worktree_failed worker.spawn starting the worker (for a satellite: the whole spawn request) spawn_failed , satellite_refused , …_unreachable worker.run worker start → its exit (restarts reopen it) exit_code , hung , the run's result pr.open gitoodo worker pr : push and pull request delivery_failed checks.wait pull request found → checks decided checks_failed , the run's result merge the merge call (or enabling auto-merge) merge_failed merge.wait auto-merge or a human merge → merged – cleanup removing the worktree and the branch after the merge (local hosts) cleanup_failed Waits are logged once per change, not on every pass: dispatch.wait (the dispatcher starts no worker: paused , no_dispatching_repo , classifier_unreachable , config_invalid , disk_low , machine_fault ) and dispatch.host_wait (an issue's os: / host: labels match no free host, with the concrete reason of #750: unknown_host , no_platform , os_mismatch , offline , agent_missing , usage_gate , login_expired (the agent says its login there no longer works, #994), low_memory , at_capacity , host_limit (the machine's own maximum, #967; detail names machine and number), global_limit , and repo_share when the repository is at its fair share of the slots, #959; detail names the wanted host= / os= and the sentence with this machine's names and the satellites) carry reason and since ; a new reason logs again with previous and previous_ms . The end of a wait is dispatch.wait_end / dispatch.host_wait_end with waited_for and waited_ms . A machine with free slots that takes no worker while ready work waits logs dispatch.host_rejected once per change, with host , reason (the furthest one over the agents that may start there, a

Gitoodo shows every text in one language, chosen in Settings → General → Language. The window, the tray menu and tooltip, system notifications, user-facing errors and chat webhook messages always follow the same language and switch together at runtime, without a restart. Supported languages Tag Language Own name Direction Intl locale de German Deutsch left to right de-DE en English English left to right en-GB zh-Hans Chinese (Simplified) 中文（简体） left to right zh-Hans-CN hi Hindi हिन्दी left to right hi-IN es Spanish Español left to right es-ES ar Arabic العربية right to left ar German is the reference shape of the catalogue; English is the fallback. Choosing the language The setting is System or one of the tags above. It is stored in settings.json ( language ) and therefore part of the settings export and import (see settings-backup.md ). The frontend mirrors it in localStorage because the texts are needed before settings.json arrives. System walks navigator.languages and takes the first supported language. Regional variants map to their language: es-MX → es , zh-CN , zh-SG and zh-Hans → zh-Hans , ar-EG → ar , de-AT → de , hi-IN → hi . Traditional Chinese ( zh-Hant , zh-TW , zh-HK , zh-MO ) and every other language fall back to English. The picker shows each language in its own name, regardless of the current language. How texts are organised src/i18n/<namespace>.ts holds German and English for one area of the app ( shell , questions , dashboard , detail , settings , filter , permissions , native , support ). src/i18n/catalogue.ts lists the namespaces. src/i18n/locales/<tag>.ts holds one further language for all namespaces. Its type is Translation , so a missing or extra key is a compile error. t("namespace.key", vars) returns a text; {name} marks a variable. Numbers passed as variables are formatted in the digits of the language. tp("namespace.key", count, vars) returns a plural text. A plural is an object with one entry per CLDR plural category the language uses ( zero , one , two , few , many , other ); Intl.PluralRules picks the entry. Arabic uses all six, Chinese only other . Dates, times, relative ages and numbers go through Intl ( formatDate , formatDateTime , formatAge , formatNumber ). Never build them by hand. Texts shown by Rust The native namespace holds the texts of the tray menu and tooltip, system notifications and chat webhook messages. The frontend resolves them in the current language and sends them with the language's digits to the set_ui_texts command at start and on every language change ( src/App.tsx ). Rust rebuilds the tray menu right away and fills the placeholders itself. Until the first push, English applies. User-facing errors reach the frontend as categories and are translated there. Right to left Arabic sets dir="rtl" and lang on the root element. To keep the layout correct in both directions: Use logical CSS properties ( margin-inline-start , padding-inline-end , inset-inline-start , text-align: start , border-inline-start ), never left / right . Horizontal motion multiplies by var(--dir-sign) ( 1 or -1 ). Icons that point along the reading direction ( back , chevron ) are listed in DIRECTIONAL in src/ui/Icon.tsx and mirrored by src/ui/Icon.css . Repository names, issue numbers, code and URLs stay left to right inside the text; wrap them in <bdi> or set dir="ltr" where they stand alone. Question format keywords The keywords of the question format ( Recommendation: , Deadline: , (yes/no) and the others in question-format.md ) are part of the machine-readable format and stay English in every language. Only their explanations in the UI are translated; answers are read in every supported language. Language on the forge What Gitoodo writes on the forge has its own setting (#980), Settings → Language → "Language on the forge" ( forge_language in settings.json ): app (default), issue or one of the six tags. A repository can override it in its repository settings → Questions ( forge_language of the repo in orchestration.json ). It covers the intake and approval questions and notes ( crates/core/src/orchestration/intake_texts.rs ), the answer hint of question headers, the fixed lines the app posts (finishing a task, the AI summary label, the suggested forward note; src/views/detail/forgeLang.ts ) and the worker brief, which names the language for question blocks, status notes and pull request texts. Code, commit messages and repository files follow the repository's own rules. app follows the app language. The services have no window, so System uses the language the window last resolved ( window_language in settings.json , written by the window, never by a settings save); before the first window, English. issue detects the language of the issue's title and body ( crates/core/src/forge_language.rs ). Code, links, mentions, issue references and identifiers are left out first. Arabic, Devanagari and Han script must make up at least 70 % of the letters (with a minimum length); Latin text needs at least eight words and enough common words of English, German or Spanish, clearly ahead of the other two. A short, mixed or other-language text falls back to the app language. The machine-read parts of the question format stay English in every case. Adding a language Add the tag to LANGS in src/i18n/define.ts (the order is the order of the picker). Add its Intl locale to LOCALES and its own name to ENDONYMS in src/i18n/index.ts . If the language is written right to left, extend direction . Map regional variants in matchLang if the base tag alone is not enough (as for Chinese). Create src/i18n/locales/<tag>.ts with export const <name>: Translation , translating every key. Give each plural the categories the language needs. Keep every {placeholder} and keep question-format keywords German. Register it in tables in src/i18n/index.ts and in the language union in src/core/types.ts . Add the variant to Language in crates/core/src/store/settings.rs (with a serde rename if the tag is not plain lowercase) and extend its test. Add the tag to SAME_AS_ENGLISH in src/i18n/i18n.test.ts with the keys that are intentionally identical to English (brand names, hosts). Run npm test : the guard checks key parity, plural categories, placeholders and untranslated values. Then check the layout in the real app at 400 px width for clipped labels. Translation style Natural and concise, as a native speaker would write a UI; no word-by-word translation. Labels must fit the 400 px window. Product name "Gitoodo" and forge names (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo) are never translated.

Gitoodo can write its settings to a JSON file, read them back on another machine or after a reinstall, and undo the last import from an automatic backup. The UI lives in Settings → Backup ( src/views/settings/BackupPage.tsx ); the logic is in crates/core/src/store/transfer.rs and the Tauri commands in src-tauri/src/transfer.rs . File format { "app": "gitoodo", "schema_version": 2, "settings": { "...": "..." } } Field Meaning app Always gitoodo ; any other value is rejected as a foreign file. schema_version Settings schema the file was written with. settings The stored settings, accounts included, without any secret value. Older files are migrated in memory on import; the preview says so. Files from a newer schema are refused instead of being guessed at. The export is written atomically, so an interrupted export never leaves a half file behind. Suggested file name: gitoodo-settings-YYYY-MM-DD.json (local date). Secrets Tokens and the chat webhook URL live only in the keychain and never appear in an export, a backup, a preview or a log line. After an import, accounts whose token is missing in this machine's keychain show a "Replace token …" action ( accounts_needing_token ). The usage statistics choice and its random install ID live in usage.json , not in the settings, so they are never exported, imported or backed up: an imported settings file leaves the statistics undecided on the new machine, and a restored backup never brings back an install ID that was deleted by switching the statistics off ( docs/privacy.md , "Usage statistics"). Import in two phases Preview ( preview_settings_import ): the file is read, validated and migrated without changing anything. The preview lists the names of changed settings (never their values), added and removed accounts, accounts without a token and whether a migration ran. Apply ( import_settings ): after the user confirms, the current settings are written to the backup first, under the settings lock. If the backup fails, nothing is replaced. Then the imported settings are saved and theme, global shortcut and sync loops restart with them. Validation beyond the field types: every account needs a non-empty, unique id, a login and an http(s) address with a host. Automatic backup and restore Every import writes the previous settings to settings.backup.json next to the settings file. settings_backup_time returns the backup's time (Unix ms) or nothing; the UI shows it or a "no backup" hint. restore_settings_backup backs up the current settings before restoring, so a restore can itself be undone. Limits and errors Reason When too_large File over 1 MiB; it is refused without reading. not_json Not valid JSON. foreign_file app is not gitoodo . newer_version Schema newer than this build supports. invalid_content Validation failed; detail capped at 200 chars. no_backup Restore without a backup. io File access or encoding failed. The frontend maps these to its own rejection keys ( rejection() in src/views/settings/transfer.ts ) and shows a calm, localised message. Import, export and restore are recorded as audit events without content. Test IDs settings-backup-export , -import , -preview , -preview-migrated , -confirm , -confirm-yes , -cancel , -status , -renew , -restore , -restore-none , -restore-time , -restore-open (all prefixed settings-backup ).

One rule for every file and folder the app reads or writes (settings, state files, backup, logs, export and import files): Follow links for reading and writing, absolute or relative, for single files and for whole folders (config/data folder, log folder). Never replace a link with a file. Atomic saves write the temp file next to the link's target and rename it over the target; the link stays. Corrupt-file recovery leaves the link in place and copies the target's content to <name>.corrupt next to the link. Never delete a link target. Log rotation of a linked gitoodo.log copies the content to .1 and empties the target; deleting rotated files removes only the link itself. Refuse where following is unsafe. A dangling link or a link loop is reported as an error ("points to ... which does not exist; nothing was written" / "loops back on itself"); nothing is created at the link's target. Logging swallows the error and retries later. Implementation: crates/core/src/links.rs ( resolve_link ), used by store/fsutil.rs and logging/writer.rs . Export and import go through the same helpers, so the path returned by the file picker may be or contain a link. Platforms Linux/macOS direct build: covered by unit tests (linked file, linked folder, relative, dangling, loop). macOS sandboxed store build: a link outside the container only works if the user granted access to its target; the scoped-folder bookmark must be created for the resolved folder. Not verified on a device (documented only). Windows: symlinks and junctions are followed by the OS for folders; file links are resolved by resolve_link . Creating them needs developer mode or admin rights, so the tests are Unix-only. Not verified on a device (documented only).

How the popover window is framed per platform and build type, and why the App Store build stays free of private API. Code: src-tauri/src/frame.rs and frame_macos.rs (native side), src/ui/tokens.css (block "Window frame"). Per platform Build Frame Corners macOS direct transparent window over Liquid Glass (macOS 26+) or the popover material rounded, 12 pt macOS App Store solid, the page paints --color-bg , normal window shadow rounded, 12 pt Windows 11 solid rounded by DWM Windows 10, Linux solid square Plain browser solid (no data-frame from the shell) n/a The shell sets data-frame="vibrancy" or data-frame="solid" on <html> through an initialization script, so the first paint already matches. Only vibrancy lets the material show through; every other value keeps the solid tokens. Store build: no private API A transparent webview needs WebKit's private key drawsBackground (wry sets it whenever Tauri asks for transparent ). App Store review rejects private API, so the store build keeps an opaque webview and only rounds the window ( Frame::Rounded ): The main window is declared with "create": false in tauri.conf.json and built in frame::create_main . Transparency and effects are only requested when frame_for(Platform::Mac, store = false) returns Vibrancy . The store build (Cargo feature store ) never calls transparent , so the private key is never touched and the frame is the normal opaque window. macOSPrivateApi stays off in every config. Corners: frame_macos::round_corners gives the window's content view a layer ( NSView.wantsLayer ) with CALayer.cornerRadius = frame::CORNER_RADIUS , cornerCurve continuous and masksToBounds , so the webview is clipped. The window turns non-opaque with a clear background ( NSWindow.isOpaque , NSWindow.backgroundColor = NSColor.clearColor ): only the clipped corners are see-through, the page still paints --color-bg behind every pixel, so the frame stays solid (also with Reduce transparency). Shadow: kept on ( NSWindow.hasShadow , then invalidateShadow ). For a non-opaque window macOS derives the shadow from the drawn pixels, so it follows the rounded corners; the square outline of the direct build does not occur here because there is no effect view in the square frame. No unsafe : the NSWindow is looked up among NSApplication.windows by comparing it with Tauri's ns_window() handle, so no raw pointer is dereferenced. All calls are safe objc2 bindings ( objc2-app-kit , objc2-quartz-core ); kCALayerCornerCurveContinuous is passed by its documented string value continuous instead of reading the extern static. No window-vibrancy setCornerRadius and no NSVisualEffectView / NSGlassEffectView in this build; translucency there is a separate spike. The string drawsBackground still exists in the binary as a constant in wry's code; that branch only runs for transparent , which the store build never requests. It is no Objective-C selector ( __objc_methname does not contain it). Public API used (Apple documentation): NSView.wantsLayer , NSView.layer , CALayer.cornerRadius , CALayer.cornerCurve , CALayer.masksToBounds , NSWindow.isOpaque , NSWindow.backgroundColor , NSColor.clearColor , NSWindow.hasShadow , NSWindow.invalidateShadow() , NSApplication.windows . macOS direct build Effects list [LiquidGlassRegular, Popover] , state Active , radius frame::CORNER_RADIUS (12 pt, mirrored as --radius-window ). Tauri applies the first effect the system supports: macOS 26 and later: NSGlassEffectView with its public cornerRadius . macOS 15 and older: NSVisualEffectView with the popover material; the corner radius goes through window-vibrancy's undocumented setCornerRadius . Acceptable only because this build is not reviewed by Apple; it is the second reason the store build stays solid. No window shadow ( shadow(false) ). macOS computes the shadow from the square window frame, not from the rounded material, which left a square dark outline around the corners. The page paints a veil over the material ( --color-window , 55 % of the solid ground) so text keeps the solid contrast values in light and dark. Dark mode adds a 1 px light inner edge so the window separates from dark wallpapers without a shadow. The veil sits on #root with border-radius: var(--radius-window) , never on body : with a transparent <html> , a body background propagates to the whole square canvas and fills the corners. Reduce transparency ( prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce ): macOS draws the material opaque and the veil switches to --color-bg , so the window is solid with the regular contrast. Windows and Linux Opaque windows with the page background. Windows 11 rounds undecorated windows itself (DWM, shadow: true from the config). Windows 10 and Linux stay square; no effect API is used there. Since the frame is solid , the page never draws an inner card here: the popover is the DWM-rounded window itself, and the detached window is a normal decorated window with the page edge to edge (checked on Windows 11, light and dark, #248). Resizing The popover keeps its tray-anchored, title-bar-free look and can still be resized by dragging any edge or corner. Code: src-tauri/src/window_size.rs , tray::place_main , core store/window.rs . Native resizing, no extra grip: the window is "resizable": true with "decorations": false . macOS: tao uses the style mask Borderless | Resizable , so AppKit offers the invisible resize edges and corners of a normal window, in both builds. Windows: tao hit-tests the undecorated window ( WM_NCHITTEST ) and, with the DWM shadow on, keeps the invisible resize borders outside the page, so every edge and corner works. Bounds: at least 400 x 320 logical points ( minWidth / minHeight in tauri.conf.json ); at most the work area of the screen the tray icon is on ( set_max_size each time the window opens). store::fit_size applies both bounds to the remembered size; on a screen smaller than the minimum the minimum wins and the placement keeps the top-left corner on screen. Size: the popover always opens in the remembered size (default 400 x 680 until the user resizes it); the page never reports a content height and nothing resizes the window on its own. Placement: tray::place_main gives the window its fitted size first and then centres it below (menu bar) or above (bottom taskbar) the tray icon with that size, clamped to the work area, so it never leaves the screen. Without an icon rect the positioner plugin places it as before. Persistence: window.json in the app config directory (logical points, versioned like the other stores, corrupt or missing file gives the default). The size is stored when the window hides and when the app quits, only if the user changed it: a size the app shrank to fit a smaller screen does not overwrite the wish for a larger one. Local to the installation: settings export and import do not carry it. Reset: Settings, General, "Window size", button settings-window-size-reset (command reset_window_size ) stores the default and resizes an open window in place at the tray icon. Frame at any size: the vibrancy material (direct build) and the content view's rounded layer (store build) resize with their views; the store build recomputes its pixel-derived shadow after every resize ( frame::resized , NSWindow.invalidateShadow() ). The page has no fixed widths; lists, detail and settings fill the extra space, centred empty states keep a readable measure. Detached window The popover can become a normal app window, for a longer look at the overview. Code: src-tauri/src/window_mode.rs , core store/detached.rs . Detach: header button shell-detach or Cmd+Shift+D (macOS) / Ctrl+Shift+D (Windows, Linux), command detach_window . The same window changes its style, so the page keeps its state: title bar, task bar entry (Dock icon on macOS), not always on top, freely resizable (at least 400 x 320, no upper bound) and no longer hidden on blur. The tray icon and its click keep working and bring the window to the front. Back: header button shell-attach , the same shortcut, or closing the window (red button, Alt+F4). The window hides and turns back into the popover; the app keeps running in the tray. Quit stays in the tray menu. Frame: position and size are stored in detached-window.json whenever the window goes back (and before quit), in logical points of the desktop. store::place_detached reopens it there when enough of it lies on a current screen (shrunk to that screen), otherwise at 900 x 700 centred on the main screen (shrunk to its work area on a smaller screen). Local to the installation like window.json . End of the onboarding (#617): its fixed, centred window (never stored as the frame) becomes the detached window in the stored frame, else the default, and stays in front ( finish_onboarding_window ); the overview and the pending introduction tour open in it, or the setup assistant after an orchestrator run. Closing it returns to the tray like any detached window. It does not switch back to the tray panel: on macOS that made the app an accessory app, which resigned it active, and the blur dismissed the freshly shown panel at once, so nothing appeared. Size: a size the user dragged is the stored frame; the popover keeps its own size in window.json , so switching back restores the popover size and switching again restores the window frame. Frame per build: the detached window always has the system title bar, shadow and corners, and its content runs edge to edge below the title bar, without the popover's inner card. Switching the mode switches the native frame too ( frame::apply_mode ): the direct macOS build swaps the rounded Liquid Glass / popover material for the square window background material (follows the active state), the store build drops its 12 pt content clip, Windows and Linux keep their solid native frame. The page drops its drawn corners and edge via data-window="detached" (tokens.css). Title bar on macOS (#617): framed windows (detached, onboarding, the test build) get a transparent title bar without its title, the page reaching up beneath it ( frame::title_bar , frame_macos::overlay_title_bar ). An empty unified toolbar makes the bar 52 pt tall, so the window buttons sit centred beside the page's top bar: the header with the lockup, or the onboarding's brand bar with the lockup and phases. The page learns it through data-titlebar="overlay" and keeps --titlebar-inset (physical left in every language) free for the buttons and --titlebar-height as its minimum height. The inset is where the zoom button ends plus 14 pt (#741): frame_macos::window_buttons_end measures it natively and hands it over as --titlebar-buttons-end when the bar switches on and after every resize (so 0 in full screen, where the buttons leave the bar); without a measurement the page assumes 80 pt (macOS 26/27). Both bars are data-tauri-drag-region="deep" : dragging moves the window, a double click zooms it, buttons keep their clicks (capability core:window:allow-start-dragging , core:window:allow-internal-toggle-maximize ). The popover switches it all off again. Windows and Linux keep the system title bar. The page learns the mode from get_window_mode and the window-mode event ( popover or detached ); in detached mode it reports its height but the window keeps the size the user chose. Test build The test build (Cargo feature test-access , "Gitoodo Test") starts with its window open and never hides it on blur, so automation can drive it without a tray click. Code: frame::framed , window_mode::place_start_window . Frame: the window is decorated (system title bar, square corners) from the start, although its logical mode stays popover so the shell-detach and shell-attach flows behave as in the normal build. frame::framed is true for it, so it gets the detached window's native frame, and the shell adds data-decorated on <html> ; tokens.css then drops the drawn corners and shadow of #root ( [data-frame="vibrancy"][data-decorated] ), so no grey strip or rounded inner card shows below the title bar (

h: Prompt timing and behaviour when denied
Notifications on macOS: prompt shown in the background (#166)
Background services read the token without a prompt (#369)
b: Which permissions Gitoodo needs on macOS and Windows, per build type, when the system asks, what the app does when the user declines, and where the decision comes from. Principle (Apple HIG "Privacy", Microsoft "Windows app privacy guidance"): ask in context, only when the feature needs it, explain calmly before the system prompt, and never block the app when a permission is denied; show a hint that leads to the system settings. Build types: macOS direct: Developer ID, hardened runtime, notarized, not sandboxed ( Entitlements.direct.plist ). macOS App Store: sandboxed ( Entitlements.appstore.plist , Cargo feature store , config overlay tauri.appstore.conf.json ). Windows direct: unpackaged installer, full trust. Windows MSIX: packaged for the Microsoft Store ( src-tauri/windows/AppxManifest.template.xml ). Matrix Purpose macOS direct macOS App Store Windows direct Windows MSIX Network to forges (HTTPS) no entitlement needed com.apple.security.network.client none capability internetClient Forge on the local network Local Network prompt ( NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription ); ATS NSAllowsLocalNetworking same, plus network.client none (firewall prompt is the system) privateNetworkClientServer Skill install into agent skills folders writes directly (not sandboxed) folder dialog ( files.user-selected.read-write ), explanation first writes directly writes directly ( runFullTrust ) Desktop control (Agent Desktop) Accessibility and Screen Recording for Agent Desktop, once per Mac; see Agent Desktop not available (no npm, no SSH in the sandbox) a signed-in, unlocked session not available in the Store build Notifications UNUserNotificationCenter , authorization at start or first send; denial shown same (sandbox needs no entitlement) no prompt; hint to Notifications settings same Start at sign-in LaunchAgent via the autostart plugin; hint to Login Items SMAppService.mainApp (macOS 13+) autostart plugin (registry) windows.startupTask , see store Menu bar / tray only, no Dock icon LSUIElement LSUIElement none none Tokens Data protection keychain (group entitlement + profile), file-based fallback; see Keychain same group; see Keychain Credential Manager, no prompt Credential Manager, no prompt Prompt timing and behaviour when denied Local network (macOS): the system asks on the first connection to a local host. The app does not pre-prompt. When the connection to a local forge fails, the wizard shows a calm note with the action "Systemeinstellungen öffnen" ( Privacy_LocalNetwork ). Only shown for local hosts on macOS ( local_network_hint_applies ). Notifications (macOS): Gitoodo asks for alert and sound authorization at start once an account and a notification type are set up, and again before every send (the system only prompts while undecided). The settings page reads the state the same way: on a denial it says so ("Mitteilungen sind ausgeschaltet"), otherwise it keeps the general note; both lead to the Notifications pane. See Notifications on macOS . Notifications (Windows, Linux): the Tauri notification plugin reports the permission as granted, so a denial cannot be detected; the page keeps the general note with the action "Systemeinstellungen öffnen" ( ms-settings:notifications ). A failed send is logged. Start at sign-in: toggled by the user on the autostart page. When it fails (denied or pending approval in Login Items), the page shows the error with the action "Systemeinstellungen öffnen" ( com.apple.LoginItems-Settings.extension , ms-settings:startupapps ). First-run onboarding (#94, #617): shown on first launch, whenever no account exists, and from "Hilfe & Feedback → Erste Schritte". It runs in its own centred window (980 x 680, clamped to the screen; its frame is never stored as the window frame) with named phases on top: Willkommen, Konto, Repos, Arbeitsweise, Mitteilungen & Start, Fertig. Enter runs the main action and Esc goes back, except in text fields. The repo step switches repos on or off with the same disabled_repos as Settings → Repos and leaves orchestration rules alone. Its notification step asks only on the button "Mitteilungen erlauben" and shows the denied hint with the Notifications pane; its autostart step (on by default) shows the same error and Login Items action as the autostart page. Progress is stored in the settings ( onboarding ), so every step can be skipped and an interrupted run resumes; closing the window pauses it and the next tray click reopens it. Finishing ("Zum Überblick", or "Orchestrator einrichten" for the setup assistant) turns the window into the regular detached window ( finish_onboarding_window , see docs/window-frame.md ), where the overview and the introduction tour (or the setup assistant) follow. Skill folder (App Store build only): the skill page explains why ~/.claude is needed and what is written (only gitoodo-questions ), then opens the folder dialog. A folder not named .claude is rejected with a hint; cancelling changes nothing. The direct build skips this step. The system settings deep links are in src-tauri/src/permissions.rs ( settings_url ). Notifications on macOS (#131) Symptom: on macOS 27 no notification appeared and Gitoodo was missing from System Settings > Notifications. Root cause: the Tauri notification plugin (2.x) posts through notify-rust and mac-notification-sys , which use the deprecated NSUserNotificationCenter . Before the first post, mac-notification-sys looks up a bundle id with an AppleScript ( get id of application ... , blocked in the sandbox and failing anyway), falls back to com.apple.Finder / com.apple.Terminal and swaps the implementation of NSBundle.bundleIdentifier . Notifications were therefore posted under another app's identity; Gitoodo never registered with Notification Center and never asked for authorization.
