The plugin spawns the post and returns success, and its desktop permission check always answers "granted", so nothing was logged. Fix: on macOS the plugin is not linked any more. src-tauri/src/notify_macos.rs uses UNUserNotificationCenter through the safe objc2-user-notifications bindings (no unsafe ): requestAuthorizationWithOptions (alert, sound), then addNotificationRequest with a unique identifier. It only runs inside an .app bundle (an unbundled cargo /dev binary would make the center raise); outside, a warning is logged and nothing is posted. Failures are logged as notification_error with a reason ( authorization_failed , rejected , no_app_bundle ), never with the notification text. Windows and Linux keep the plugin and now log a failed send. Limits: the error object of a failed request is not read (that would need unsafe ), so the log has the reason but not the system's error code. The permission state comes from the authorization answer, because reading UNNotificationSettings from its completion handler also needs unsafe . There is no notification-center delegate, so a banner may be held back while Gitoodo's own window is in front. Notifications on macOS: prompt shown in the background (#166) Symptom: after #131 the permission request did not appear and Gitoodo was missing from System Settings > Notifications. Evidence (unified log of the installed, Developer ID signed, sandboxed /Applications/Gitoodo.app , macOS 27.2): usernoted registers the bundle at the first request ("Sending request for permission for <bundle id>"), but the prompt record is alertStyle:"none" with response action: closed and the settings read authorizationStatus: Denied ; the authorization was only set to "allow" seven seconds later, by hand. Signing, bundle identity and sandbox are therefore fine: the center is reached ( Creating a user notification center , didGrant ) and later banners were delivered ( Presenting ... alertStyle:"banner" ). The app log has no notification_* event because nothing failed. Cause: the request is made at start from a menu-bar app ( LSUIElement , accessory policy) that is not the active app, so the system shows the prompt as a quiet banner that closes by itself. It is counted as not allowed, and the user never saw a dialog. Fix: the first authorization request of an installation (marker file notification-prompted in the config dir, notify::first_prompt ) activates the app first ( NSApplication.activate , main thread, safe bindings), so the prompt is shown to the user. Later requests stay silent. Not reproducible here without wiping the notification database, so the fresh-install check (prompt visible, entry in System Settings > Notifications, question and #73 reminder as banners) needs a human on a clean install. Open: without a notification-center delegate a banner is still held back while Gitoodo's own window is in front (needs unsafe , which the crate forbids). Keychain Tokens and the chat webhook URL live in the OS credential store ( crates/core/src/secrets.rs ). On macOS the app uses the data protection keychain (#126): items belong to a keychain access group and carry no per-app access list, so the direct, App Store and dev builds that share the group read the same token without any prompt (TN3137, "Sharing access to keychain items"). The group is Q7V3X27S2U.de.gitoodo.app (team id plus bundle id), the first keychain-access-groups entry, hence the default group of new items; the code sets no group. The direct build lists the group of the former identifier online.lindstedt.gitoodo (Gitoodo 0.1.x, #595) second, only so the one-time move ( crates/core/src/identity_migration.rs ) can copy the tokens out of it without a prompt; its Developer ID profile allows Q7V3X27S2U.* . Remove that entry once no 0.1.x install is left ( scripts/check-identifier.py allows exactly this line). Items of older versions live in the file-based keychain and are described below. Entitlements. keychain-access-groups is restricted: the data protection keychain needs keychain-access-groups or com.apple.application-identifier , and both must be authorized by an embedded provisioning profile (TN3125, TN3137). A signed app that claims them without a matching profile is killed at launch, so they are not in the default plists. The extra plists ( Entitlements.direct.keychain.plist , Entitlements.appstore.keychain.plist ) and the overlays src-tauri/tauri.keychain.direct.conf.json / tauri.keychain.appstore.conf.json (add --config after the usual config) set the entitlements and embed the profile from src-tauri/profiles/{direct,appstore}.provisionprofile (ignored by git, account specific). The sandbox of the store build needs no further keychain entitlement. Without the profile (plain build, dev, ad hoc) the app gets errSecMissingEntitlement (-34018) and uses only the file-based keychain; the prompt hint stays. Builds with the entitlement keep a shared copy there for exactly these builds (see "Migration and mixed builds"). Profiles (Apple Developer account). Created 2026-11-10 through the App Store Connect API (global key in ~/.config/appstoreconnect/api_key.json , POST /v1/bundleIds and POST /v1/profiles , types MAC_APP_DIRECT with the Developer ID Application certificate and MAC_APP_STORE with the Apple Distribution certificate); the portal steps below are the manual equivalent. The App ID did not exist yet and was created with the same call. The App Store profile expires 2027-04-19 with its certificate and must be recreated then. Since #595 (2026-11-16) the App IDs are de.gitoodo.app and de.gitoodo.app.service with Developer ID profiles for both; an App Store profile for de.gitoodo.app does not exist yet: Identifiers: App ID de.gitoodo.app exists; no extra capability is needed for keychain sharing on macOS (the group is derived from the team id and the profile's application identifier). Profiles, "Developer ID" (macOS): create a Developer ID provisioning profile for the App ID with the Developer ID Application certificate; save as src-tauri/profiles/direct.provisionprofile . Profiles, "Mac App Store Connect": create a profile for the same App ID with the Apple Distribution certificate; save as src-tauri/profile

t: Test access: driving the app without a human
h: A real test repository beside the fixture
Check that every element has a test ID
Restore the desktop after a test
b: The normal app is a tray panel: no window until a tray click, dismissed on blur, hidden from the accessibility tree. The test access build removes those obstacles so a worker can operate it with Agent Desktop ( agent-desktop , see below). It is a separate Cargo feature ( test-access ); release and store builds contain none of it. What the test build changes: Window mode : a regular, decorated window, visible at start, never dismissed on blur. The app is a Dock app, so agent-desktop list-windows lists it as Gitoodo Test . It opens in the detached window's frame (remembered, else 900 x 700 centred, clamped to the screen; #363), not in the popover size ( docs/window-frame.md , "Test build"). Own identity : bundle ID de.gitoodo.app.testaccess , own config and log directory. It runs next to the installed app and never touches it (single instance, keychain, settings). Test account : a fixture forge ( fixture/demo , user tester ) and an in-memory token store. No real token, no network, no keychain. The account keeps the fixed id acc-fixture across restarts, so per-account state such as folded groups persists; other accounts are removed. Test IDs in the accessibility tree : each data-testid is mirrored into the DOM id (Agent Desktop's native_id of kind ax_dom_identifier , searchable with find --native-id ) and into aria-roledescription . An element that already has its own id (label association) keeps it. Notifications : the permission reads as granted; posts are logged as test_notification . Usage statistics : hard stop. The test build, like any run with GITOODO_UI_AUTOMATION=1 , records, writes and sends nothing, whatever the onboarding switch says ( docs/privacy.md ). Build and start VITE_TEST_ACCESS=1 npx tauri build --debug --bundles app \ --features test-access --config src-tauri/tauri.test-access.conf.json open -n "target/debug/bundle/macos/Gitoodo Test.app" The panel is open right away. Nothing needs a tray click. Address elements by test ID Scripts use Agent Desktop. Point GITOODO_AGENT_DESKTOP at it (default: agent-desktop on PATH, which Gitoodo installs as ~/.local/bin/agent-desktop ); the scripts in this repo never hardcode its location. Workers go through gitoodo desktop [--on NAME] <command> instead, which waits for their turn at that machine's desktop and reaches another machine's desktop over SSH ( dispatcher ). agent-desktop find --app "Gitoodo Test" --native-id shell-settings --first # exact test ID agent-desktop click @<snapshot>:e<n> # ref from the line above Every command prints one JSON envelope; matches carry ref_id ( @<snapshot>:e<n> ), role , name and native_id . Refs belong to one snapshot; the test ID does not change. snapshot --app "Gitoodo Test" prints the whole tree ( --max-depth 50 for deep screens). Ref actions are headless: they neither move the pointer nor take the focus. Look again after each action. One session at a time uses a desktop. Workers take turns through gitoodo desktop-turn ; a script is run while nobody else uses this desktop. Fixture content: three questions in fixture/demo . #1 has a question block with a deadline (tomorrow), #2 is free text, #3 has a deadline two days in the past (the overdue label of the list, #73). GITOODO_TEST_EXTRA_QUESTIONS=<n> at start adds n free-form questions (#4 on, at most 200) to check many open questions (#237). Rows are questions-row-… , copy and share buttons are questions-copy-… and questions-share-… , the detail screen uses detail-… . For long-string layout checks (#337), set GITOODO_TEST_LONG_TEXT=1 . Every fixture title (default and scale mode) gains a long sentence and one long word without break opportunities, so wrapping, clipping and ellipses show at the minimum window size. Bodies, numbers and labels stay unchanged. For large-list navigation (#337), set both GITOODO_TEST_REPOS=300 and GITOODO_TEST_ISSUES_PER_REPO=5 in the test app's launch environment. This replaces the default fixture with 300 repositories ( fixture/scale-001 through fixture/scale-300 ) and 1,500 distinct issues. Each issue is assigned to tester , has needs-human and a cycling ready , in-progress , in-review or blocked status label. Question bodies reuse the three default question types. Each repo also has two fixture pulls, with the green pull linked to that repo's first issue. Dashboard groups and counts come through the normal Rust adapter and sync path. Both values must be positive integers; missing, invalid or zero input keeps the default fixture and its existing extra-question behavior. Valid scale inputs are capped at 300 repos and 20 issues per repo (6,000 issues total); GITOODO_TEST_EXTRA_QUESTIONS is ignored in scale mode. The scale dataset is seeded once at startup. Repo names, forge IDs and issue URLs are unique; issue numbers are globally unique within this fixture. Comments and closures are scoped to their repository and remain in memory until exit. Other unsupported adapter mutations stay unsupported. This creates test data, not a performance result; navigation and responsiveness still need an explicit runtime check. Showcase data for screenshots GITOODO_TEST_FIXTURE_LANG=de or =en replaces the fixture with an invented open-source team in that language ( src-tauri/src/test_showcase.rs ): two repositories ( kiezwerk/pegelstand and kiezwerk/radkeller , in English harborlight/tidewatch and harborlight/trailkit ), four questions to the user (one with a deadline tomorrow, one free text, one overdue, one approval), the board with three running workers, pull requests (one with a failing ci/test ), a week of closed issues and merged pulls for the weekly review, eight weeks of throughput, the readiness checklist of a well kept repo and a scripted orchestrator chat that proposes one comment. Workers, usage, setup checks and the chat are answered by the fixture, never by a running classifier, dispatcher or agent. A simulated dispatcher ( src-tauri/src/test_showcase_dispatcher.rs , #915) gives each session a live terminal over the real attach protocol (backlog, a step line every few seconds, typed keys echo back) and applies steering: Hold and Resume mark the worker held, an instruction appears in its terminal, Cancel, Stop and Park end it, Restart counts a restart. Any other value keeps the plain fixture above. GITOODO_TEST_SHOWCASE_SESSIONS=N (with the showcase) runs N sessions in total instead of three, at most 24: the extra ones are in-progress issues numbered from 300 in both repositories, for checks of a crowded session grid. GITOODO_TEST_WEEKLY_REVIEW=1 (with the showcase) makes the weekly review due at start. The status bar shows the version only in every build; commit and build time are on the About page. The landing page's shots in site/shots/ come from the browser demo ( scripts/site-shots.mjs ). The test build still reads services and files outside its config dir (the classifier socket, the dispatcher, state_dir ). For recordings, point GITOODO_STATE_DIR , GITOODO_CONFIG_DIR and GITOODO_BIN_DIR at an empty temporary folder so nothing of an installed Gitoodo shows up or is touched. A real test repository beside the fixture For flows the fixture cannot show (a real clone, worktree and agent session, e.g. "Solve with an agent", #919), an account of the test config may reach its real forge: add it to settings.json of the test config dir and hand its token to the test app in the launch environment as GITOODO_TOKEN_<ID> (the id in upper case, other characters as _ , as for a headless service; docs/daemon.md ). Start the binary directly (not open --env ), so the token is not in an argument list. Such an account stays across starts and uses the real forge adapter; an account without the variable is removed as before, and the showcase never keeps one. The keychain is never read or written. Point GITOODO_STATE_DIR , GITOODO_LOG_DIR and GITOODO_BIN_DIR at a temporary folder, set the repository's local_path and dispatch.worktree_root in the test config's orchestration.json to that folder too, and run your own gitoodo classifier (and gitoodo dispatcher , with a stub agent first on PATH ) with the same variables and GITOODO_CONFIG_DIR set to the test config dir before the app starts: the test build shares the service labels with an installed release, so it would otherwise ask the release's services. Use a dedicated test repository only. Optional native navigation measurements (#337) Add VITE_TEST_PERFORMANCE=1 alongside VITE_TEST_ACCESS=1 to the build command. Both build flags are required; the dynamically imported probe is excluded from normal builds. Runtime automation alone does not enable it. Launch the scale fixture as above. Before the actual run, calibrate accessibility visibility in the real test app: use agent-desktop snapshot --app "Gitoodo Test" --max-depth 50 and reconstruct the readonly report fields as described below, then perform one native input and read them after a quiet pause. If the platform omits this offscreen field or its value, the measurement is not validated. Restart the test process after calibration; only a fresh process resets it. The probe counts trusted keydown , pointerdown , wheel and actual scroll events. Scroll includes browser-generated scroll events, including programmatic scrolling; trust alone does not prove a human caused a scroll. Non-trusted events and non-finite, zero, negative or future timestamps are rejected. Timestamps must share the performance.now() time origin. It records event timestamp to next animation callback scheduling latency , and gaps between animation callbacks during an input/scroll burst and its 250 ms quiet tail. These are neither pixel-paint/full-response latency nor displayed FPS. A delayed callback can extend that tail; no idle loop runs afterward. Use a foreground, visible window and record the native actions, dataset and environment with the result. No pass/fail threshold is inferred from these numbers. Read the fields only after the burst is quiet: reporting updates values and creates any additional fragment fields after sampling stops, without live announcements, focus changes or page layout changes. The JSON contains accepted counts by event type, rejected counts, pending queue overflow, burst count, elapsed process window and accumulated active window in milliseconds. eventToNextRafSchedulingMs and frameGapMs each include observed/retained/dropped counts and nearest-rank p50/p95/max of the first 4,096 retained samples (zero when empty). Pending event timestamps also cap at 4,096; overflow events are counted but not measured. Results are cumulative until process exit. No targets, key values, content, account data, network requests or logs are collected. The probe adds measurement overhead; corroborate the numbers with native navigation observations, rather than treating them as paint proof. The accessibility helper caps individual values at 120 characters. Read the header test-performance and test-performance-part-0 through parts - 1 using a full snapshot (without -i ). Each part is sequence:index:fragment with at most 96 characters of JSON. Require every sequence to match the header, join fragments by index and check the header character count before parsing. Discard mixed or incomplete reads; do not focus the fields to read them. The report is published only after a quiet burst. The installed store preview (#235) The signed, sandboxed store preview has no test build features, but it has one runtime switch: start it with GITOODO_UI_AUTOMATION=1 in its environment. Without the variable nothing differs from a normal start (no visible change, no permission prompt). osascript -e 'quit app "Gitoodo"' # single instance: a running app ignores the variable open -n --env GITOODO_UI_AUTOMATION=1 /Applications/Gitoodo.app "${GITOODO_AGENT_DESKTOP:-agent-desktop}" find --app Gitoodo --native-id shell-root --first With the switch on, the app is a regular (Dock) app so the accessibility API lists it, the real borderless popover opens at start (no tray click) and

t: Privacy policy: feedback and usage statistics
b: Single source for the privacy policy text of the app and the website (sections "Feedback" and "Usage statistics"). All outgoing connections of the app are listed in privacy-network-inventory.md . Publisher and controller: the GbR behind Gitoodo (contact: the GbR mailbox named in the imprint). Rationale for the feedback rules: Microsoft Store policy 10.5.2 (data is shared only after opt-in). The usage statistics are on by default by the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-16, in every build. Principle Feedback is submitted only when you press Send . Nothing is published, and there are no automatic feedback prompts. After you submit, queued messages are retried automatically for up to 24 hours. Store builds may show the system's own rating request now and then; Settings → System turns it off or stops it for good. Sending is opt-in per message ; nothing you chose for one message carries over to the next. What is sent Data When Your text and the category Always, because it is the message itself Technical details Only if you tick it for this message (preview shown) Logs Only if you tick it for this message (preview shown) Screenshots Only if you attach them for this message (preview shown) Reply address Only if you enter one; off by default App version Always, so we know which build the message is about Message ID Always; random per message, lets retries arrive only once Tokens, hosts and accounts are never sent. You see a preview of exactly what will be sent before you press Send. Path and processors The app sends the message to the GbR's own relay. The relay sits behind Cloudflare (traffic passes Cloudflare's network). The relay forwards it by email to the GbR mailbox. Processors: Cloudflare, the mail provider the relay uses to send, and the mail provider hosting the recipient mailbox (GbR). Log and retention The relay stores no message content. It logs only metadata: sender ID (public application ID), time, reference ID, result, size and a daily-salted IP hash (not reversible, changes every day). Metadata is deleted after 14 days . For abuse protection and safe retries it also keeps, for at most 24 hours, rate-limit counters per salted IP hash and the message ID with its reference. The received email stays in the GbR mailbox until the matter is handled and is used only to answer you and improve Gitoodo. The app keeps an unsent draft on your device. After you submit a message, temporary delivery failures place that message and its selected details in the local outbox. Retries stop after 24 hours. Finished outbox entries are removed after seven days while the app is running; when the app is closed, cleanup happens on its next start. The editable draft remains until successful delivery or until you clear it. Reply contact A reply address is optional and off by default. Without it we cannot answer you. It is used only to reply to this message. Website contact form The website ( site/ , privacy page section "Contact form") has its own form on the same relay, with the browser sender gitoodo-web ( gitoodo-web-test for local previews). Only when the visitor presses Send does the browser post the message, the chosen category, the reply address if entered, and the page's language and path (no query) to relay.silvio-und-maik.de ; nothing else, no technical details, logs or screenshots. Path, processors, log and retention are the same as above, except that the logged sender ID is the fixed website sender, not an installation ID. To block abuse the relay counts requests per HMAC-hashed IP address for one hour. In the browser the form stores only the flag gitoodo.site.contact.greeted (greeting seen or closed) in localStorage; the draft lives in memory while the page is open. Without JavaScript or if the relay is unreachable, the page offers the GbR mailbox instead. Your rights Access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection and complaint to a supervisory authority under GDPR. Write to the GbR mailbox and quote the reference ID shown after sending. Usage statistics Gitoodo can send anonymous usage statistics so we can see how the app is used and improve it for the people who use it. The statistics are on by default , and you can switch them off at any time. Default and switching off The last onboarding step shows the switch "Help make Gitoodo better", on by default, with what is sent and what never is. You can switch it off right there; "Finish" stores your choice. Settings → General has the same switch at any time. Nothing is sent before "Finish" stores the choice. Installs without a stored choice (installs that finished onboarding before this feature, or an onboarding that was closed early) send nothing, and Settings → General shows the switch off for them; they are not switched on silently. Running the introduction again from Help shows the switch on and stores it at "Finish". Running the introduction again shows the stored choice; it never resets it to the default. The setup steps you go through before the last step are held in memory only . When "Finish" stores "on" they are sent with their original times; when it stores "off", or when the app quits first, they are dropped. Switching off (on the last onboarding step or in Settings → General) stops sending at once (a request on its way is cancelled), deletes the install ID and drops everything still queued. Switching on again starts with a new install ID. The choice is stored per installation in usage.json in the app's config folder. It is not part of the settings export, import or backup. What is measured Only fixed identifiers from one list in the code ( crates/core/src/usage/taxonomy.rs ), never free text. A test checks every possible event against a parameter whitelist. Onboarding: which step was shown, left with next, skip or back, or closed (step name only); the token wizard page and the token check result per forge type; the error kind when a repo list could not load; which setup parts were done, skipped or failed. Use: which views, help entries and help center topics are opened; whether the introduction tour was finished or skipped and the weekly review was dismissed or switched off; that a question was forwarded (never to whom); slash command names of Gitoodo's own commands (an agent's commands count only as "agent"); answers by kind (card or comment, with or without AI help); the result of the system check; error kinds of failed commands and background services; counts of chat messages, started workers and merged pull requests. Milestones, once per install: first question seen, first answer sent, first worker started, first pull request merged, first chat message. An app start event and one "alive" event per day. Context of each visit: app version, build variant (direct macOS, Mac App Store, Windows installer, Microsoft Store, Linux), operating system and architecture, mode (direct or orchestrator), UI language, the forge types in use (Forgejo, Gitea, GitHub, GitLab), whether they are cloud hosts, self-hosted or both, the orchestrator agent type, the number of accounts and enabled repos as a range (for example "6-20"), the install week and the install age as a range of days. Pages are synthetic addresses such as app://gitoodo/board ; no referrer is sent. What is never measured Contents of issues, pull requests, comments, answers, questions or chats. Names of repos, accounts, organisations, labels, branches or people. Tokens, passwords, keys or webhook addresses. Addresses of your forge servers or other hosts (only "cloud", "self-hosted" or "mixed"). Free text of any kind, including error messages (only the error kind). Install ID A random 16-digit hexadecimal ID is created when the choice "on" is stored ("Finish" with the switch on, or switching it on in Settings) and links the events of this installation. It is stored only in usage.json , is deleted when you switch the statistics off and is replaced by a new one when you switch them on again. It is not derived from the device, the account or any other identifier, and it is a different ID from the sender ID of the feedback relay: the two cannot be joined. Forgejo check Forgejo and Gitea share one API. To tell them apart for the forge type, Gitoodo asks each self-hosted Gitea-type server once, without a token, for /api/forgejo/v1/version and keeps only the answer "Forgejo" or "Gitea". This happens only while the statistics are on; the server address itself is never sent to the statistics server. Path, processing and retention Events go in batches, at the latest every 15 minutes, by HTTPS to the GbR's own Matomo instance at matomo.silvio-und-maik.de (server in the EU). No third party receives them. Offline, up to 500 events wait locally in usage.json ; events older than 23 hours are dropped instead of being sent late. The app sets no cookies. Matomo stores IP addresses only shortened (IPv4 by two bytes, IPv6 correspondingly); the full address is used only while the request is processed, for the country lookup. Raw visit data is deleted on the Matomo instance after 180 days ; only aggregated reports remain. Because the install ID is random and deleted when you switch the statistics off, switching off ends any link between future and past events. Builds without a statistics site ID (development builds, forks), the test access build, UI automation runs and the browser demo record and send nothing. Your rights for the statistics Switching off in Settings → General ends all sending. Access, deletion and objection under GDPR: write to the GbR mailbox.

Usage statistics in detail Fail closed: without GITOODO_MATOMO_SITE_ID at build time ( crates/core/src/usage/mod.rs , SITE_ID ), nothing is recorded or sent. Development builds and forks therefore send nothing. Site ID 17 ("Gitoodo App") only in distributed builds: scripts/build-local-mac.sh (and so scripts/release-mac.sh , which calls it) sets it for the signed Developer ID build; src-tauri/windows/package.ps1 sets it only for a package with the real store identity (not Gitoodo.LocalTest ); the Mac App Store submission build passes it on the command line. An explicitly set value wins; GITOODO_MATOMO_SITE_ID= (empty, macOS) or -NoUsageStatistics (Windows) builds without statistics. npm run tauri dev , debug builds, the test access build and the CI gate never get it. The dimensions are listed in crates/core/src/usage/context.rs . Retention: raw visit data is deleted on the instance after 180 days. Hard stop: UI automation ( GITOODO_UI_AUTOMATION ), the test access build ( test-access feature) and the browser demo ( src/platform/browser.ts ) never record, write or send, whatever the stored choice. Choice gate: until a choice is stored ("Finish" on the last onboarding step, switch on by default, or the switch in Settings) the tracker only holds onboarding events in memory (at most 200); everything else is dropped. An install without a stored choice sends nothing; the core never assumes the default. "Off" drops them, deletes the install ID and the queue, and cancels a request in flight. Tests: crates/core/src/usage/tracker.rs . Payload whitelist: each request carries only idsite , rec , apiv , send_image , _id , _idts , rand , url , cdt , e_c , e_a , e_n , e_v and dimension1 - dimension12 ; no urlref , no uid , no cip , no token_auth . Test: crates/core/src/usage/payload.rs . Queue: at most 500 events in usage.json , batches of 100 by bulk POST, events older than 23 hours dropped (Matomo would need a token for older times). Store builds behave like direct builds and report their own variant ( mas , msix ); the request goes through the sandbox's outgoing network entitlement the app already has for forges. 3. Local only Loopback and local files only: the notification and tray integration, the keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Secret Service), the local log, usage.json , rating.json and the settings file.

Gitoodo can report new questions to a chat through an outgoing webhook (Slack, Teams, or Matrix/generic). It is off by default. Settings: type, webhook URL, on/off, "send question text", "daily digest", the login-to-handle mapping for mentions, and "send test message". Secret handling The webhook URL is a secret. It lives only in the keychain (service gitoodo , key chat-webhook ), never in the settings file, an export, a log line or an error text. The frontend can only ask "configured yes/no"; the URL is write-only. Failures are reported as a category ( invalid , not_configured , unreachable , timeout , tls , status , keychain ) and logged with the host only. All network access is in crates/core/src/chat . Message Repo, title, deadline and a link to the issue. The question text is added only with the option "send question text" (default off) and is cut at 500 characters. Payload per type: Type Body Slack {"text": ...} (mrkdwn) Teams message with one Adaptive Card 1.4 attachment Matrix / generic {"text": ..., "html": ...} (plain text and escaped HTML, for hooks) Mentions A message mentions the person asked: the login in the header of the question's first addressed block, or the new person of a forward. The settings map forge logins to chat handles; the mapping is not a secret and lives in the settings file ( chat.handles ). Logins match in any case. A login without a usable handle gets no mention. A handle must not contain blanks, control characters or < > & " | , and is at most 128 characters; at most 200 mappings are kept. Type Handle Written as Slack member ID U… / W… , user group ID S… <@U…> , <!subteam^S…> ; anything else as plain @handle Teams sign-in address (UPN) or Entra object ID <at>handle</at> plus a mention entity in msteams Matrix user ID @user:server link pill to https://matrix.to/#/@user:server ; else text Forwards Forwarding a question (see docs/question-format.md , "Forwarding") sends one message "Question forwarded: <title>" with repo, link and the mention of the new person, never the question text. It counts against the same hourly limit; in digest mode it becomes a digest line. Daily digest With "daily digest" (default off) new questions are not sent one by one. They are queued in chat-notified.json and sent as one message once a day has passed since the first queued item: a title with the count, then one line per question with title, repo, link and mention (at most 20 lines, then "+N"). The digest never carries the question text. The queue survives a restart; the rules below (once per question, no replay, hourly limit) still apply. Delivery rules At most once per question: a question is marked as reported before it is sent and the mark is persisted ( chat-notified.json ), so a restart never repeats it. A failed send is not repeated. No replay: a question waiting longer than 1 hour is marked as reported without sending. This covers offline gaps, the first poll after a restart and the moment the feature is enabled. Such questions are dropped, not caught up. Bursts: per poll at most 3 single messages; the rest is one summary message ("N more questions"). Rate limit: at most 20 messages per hour, 1 s between messages; the excess is dropped and logged. Errors: exactly one attempt, no retry. After a failure the rest of that batch is dropped. The warning is throttled. Removing an account forgets its marks and its queued digest lines.

Gitoodo asks, rarely and quietly, whether someone wants to support its development. Supporting unlocks nothing; every feature works the same without it. The wording is "Unterstützen" / "support", never "Spende" / "donation" (the publisher is not a charity and issues no receipts). Where Settings : the row "Entwicklung unterstützen" with a pink heart ( settings-support ) opens the support page. It is always there, also after "Nicht mehr fragen". Footer heart ( footer-support ): a small pink heart at the trailing end of the status footer, in every view, opens the same page; label and tooltip "Entwicklung unterstützen". It is permanent and quiet (no badge, no counter, no animation) and does not count as an ask: the rules below stay unchanged. Inline ask ( support-ask ): a card above the tab list after an answer was sent from the detail view, i.e. at the place of the success. No dialog, no focus move, nothing blocked. Its three actions: open the page ( support-ask-open ), "Später" ( support-ask-later ), "Nicht mehr fragen" ( support-ask-never ). Weekly review ( weekly-review-ask , #707): when the ask is due, the weekly review card (see below) may carry it instead, with the same three actions and the same wording; without payment links (Mac App Store or unknown channel) the text names only a star or a recommendation. When the card shows Rules live in src/views/support/logic.ts (pure functions, tested with simulated time). Rule Value Earliest ask next success after 3 successes Successes spread over at least 2 different local days Asks per installation, at most 3 Pause after showing or "Später" 90 days Pause after opening a payment link 270 days "Nicht mehr fragen" final, no further asks A success is an answer sent successfully from the detail view. Showing the card already counts as an ask and starts the 90-day pause, so a card closed by navigating away is not shown again on the next answer. Pauses only ever grow, never shorten. A payment click is never treated as a payment; the app does not know and does not track whether anyone paid. One prompt per session, shared cap (#707, #712). The inline ask, the weekly review and the store rating request share one cap, kept by the Rust core ( crates/core/src/asks.rs , ledger in asks.json ): at most one prompt per app session, and at least 14 days between two asks in both directions. Whichever claims it first is the only prompt until the next start. The inline card claims the cap through claim_support_ask , and only when its own rules ( askAllowed ) already allow an ask; with a closed cap the success still counts but no card shows. The weekly review claims it through claim_review ( offerReview in src/views/support/logic.ts ). It always takes the session's one prompt. It carries the ask only when reviewAsk allows it (the same askAllowed limits) and 14 days have passed since the last ask; then it counts as a support ask in the shared cap and is recorded with recordAsk (one ask, 90-day pause), exactly like the inline card. A review without the ask does not start the 14-day spacing, otherwise the weekly card would hold every other ask. Answers to the card ("Später", "Nicht mehr fragen", a payment link) only change support.json ; they never reach the cap or the rating state (no review gating). The thresholds are a hypothesis for this app: answering questions is rarer than the operations other apps count, so "3 answers over 2 days" stands for experienced use. Revisit them if the card turns out to come too early or never. Weekly review Once a week a calm card ( weekly-review ) appears above the list: answered questions, median answer time, merged pull requests and closed issues of the last 7 days, computed on the device from the user's own forge data ( loop_metrics , see docs/metrics.md ). Rules live in src/views/review/model.ts (pure, tested): On by default; "Wochenrückblick" in Settings → Notifications ( settings-weekly-review ) or "Wochenrückblick ausschalten" on the card switches it off ( weekly_review in settings.json ). The first start only remembers the current week; the first review comes the week after. The week starts on the region's first weekday. The week it was offered in is kept in localStorage ( gitoodo.weeklyReview.week ); "Schließen" ends it for that week. A week without answers, merges or closed issues shows nothing and counts as done. When another prompt already showed in this session, the review waits for a later session of the same week. Channels (fail-closed) supportChannel() maps the build variant ( build_variant command) to a channel; supportWays() decides what the page shows. Channel Payment links Star and share Direct download (macOS outside the App Store) PayPal, Ko-fi, GitHub Sponsors; Buy Me a Coffee behind "Weitere Wege" yes Windows installer and Microsoft Store (MSIX) same as direct (Microsoft Store Policy 10.8.2 allows third-party payments) yes Mac App Store none, and no mention of them in any text (Guideline 3.1.1) yes Any other OS, unknown build, or still loading none yes Addresses The default payment addresses live in one file, src/views/support/destinations.ts ; the app reads them through src/views/support/links.ts , and the project URL is shared with the About section. The landing page imports the same file and the app's support texts ( src/i18n/support.ts and its locales) in every site language. GitHub's "Sponsor" button ( .github/FUNDING.yml ) and the README's "Support" section cannot import it; tests/support-links.test.ts fails when either drifts from it. A distributor can replace or clear each payment address at build time: VITE_SUPPORT_PAYPAL_URL , VITE_SUPPORT_KOFI_URL , VITE_SUPPORT_GITHUB_URL , VITE_SUPPORT_BMAC_URL . An empty value or anything that is not https:// counts as missing: the way is hidden and the page names what is missing ( support-missing ). The project has no NETWORK.md . The support feature adds these external addresses; they are only opened in the external browser on a click, never fetched by the app: https://www.paypal.com/donate/… https://ko-fi.com/silviol https://github.com/sponsors/silvio-l https://buymeacoffee.com/silvio.lindstedt the project URL (star) Provider logos are local SVGs in src/assets/support/ (origin and licence in its README); no hotlinking, no third-party scripts or widgets. Storage The ask state (successes, days, asks, pause, declined) is stored by the Rust core in support.json in the app data directory ( crates/core/src/store/support.rs ), read leniently and written atomically. The shared ask cap lives in asks.json ( crates/core/src/store/asks.rs ). Neither file is part of the settings export, and neither is part of the usage statistics ( docs/privacy.md ). There is no payment code.
